列傳第三十四臧質魯爽沈攸之
Biographies 34: Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, and Shen Youzhi
2
臧質，字含文，東莞莒人。 父熹，字義和，武敬皇后弟也。 與兄燾並好經籍。 隆安初，兵革屢起，熹乃習騎射，志在立功。 嘗至溧陽，溧陽令阮崇與熹共獵，值虎突圍，獵徒並奔散，熹直前射之，應弦而倒。 高祖入京城，熹族子穆斬桓脩。 進至京邑，桓玄奔走，高祖使熹入宮收圖書器物，封閉府庫。 有金飾樂器，高祖問熹：「卿得無欲此乎？ 」熹正色曰：「皇上幽逼，播越非所。 將軍首建大義，劬勞王家。 雖復不肖，無情於樂。 」高祖笑曰：「聊以戲卿爾。 」行參高祖鎮軍事，員外散騎侍郎，重參鎮軍軍事，領東海太守。 以建義功封始興縣五等侯。 又參高祖車騎、中軍軍事。 高祖將征廣固，議者多不同。 熹從容言曰：「公若淩威北境，拯其塗炭，寧一六合，未為無期。 」高祖曰：「卿言是也。 」及行，熹求從，不許，以為建威將軍、臨海太守。 郡經兵寇，百不存一，熹綏緝綱紀，招聚流散，歸之者千餘家。 孫季高海道襲廣州，路由臨海，熹資給發遣，得以無乏。 徵拜散騎常侍，母憂去職。 頃之，討劉毅，起為寧朔將軍，從征。 事平，高祖遣朱齡石統大眾伐蜀，命熹奇兵出中水，以本號領建平、巴東二郡太守。 蜀主譙縱遣大將譙撫之萬餘人屯牛脾，又遣譙小苟重兵塞打鼻。 熹至牛脾，撫之戰敗退走，追斬之。 小苟聞撫之死，即便奔散。 成都既平，熹遇疾。 義熙九年，卒於蜀郡牛脾縣，時年三十九。 追贈光祿勳。
Zang Zhi, courtesy name Hanwen, was from Ju in Dongguan commandery. His father Zang Xi, courtesy name Yihe, was a younger brother of Empress Dowager Wujing. He and his elder brother Tao both devoted themselves to the classics. When warfare broke out repeatedly at the start of the Long'an era, Xi took up horsemanship and archery, determined to win distinction in battle. Once, while hunting with Liyang magistrate Ruan Chong, a tiger broke through the beaters' ring. The party scattered in panic, but Xi rode straight at the beast and dropped it with a single arrow. When Emperor Gaozu entered the capital, Xi's kinsman Zang Mu slew Huan Xiu. As the army reached the capital, Huan Xuan fled. Gaozu sent Xi into the palace to gather books, ritual objects, and furnishings and to seal the imperial storehouses. Among the treasures were gold-inlaid musical instruments. Gaozu asked Xi, "You wouldn't want these for yourself, would you?" Xi answered gravely, "The emperor is held captive and driven from his rightful seat. You, General, were first to raise the righteous cause and labor for the house of Liu. Unworthy though I am, I have no taste for music now." Gaozu laughed. "I was only teasing you." Xi was then made staff officer on Gaozu's Pacifying Army staff, Attendant Cavalier Outside the Regulars, and again staff officer on that army, while also serving as Administrator of Donghai. For his service in the founding campaign he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Shixing county. He also served on Gaozu's Chariots-and-Cavalry and Central Army staffs. When Gaozu prepared to campaign against Guanggu, many at court opposed the plan. Xi said calmly, "If you carry your authority to the northern marches and rescue those people from misery, the unification of the realm may come sooner than many think." Gaozu said, "You are right." When the army marched, Xi asked to go along but was refused; instead he was made General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Linhai. The commandery had been ravaged by war until scarcely one household in a hundred remained. Xi restored law and order, gathered the displaced, and brought more than a thousand families back. When Sun Jigao raided Guangzhou by sea, his fleet passed through Linhai; Xi supplied and provisioned the expedition so that it wanted for nothing. He was summoned to court as Regular Attendant Cavalier but resigned when his mother died. Soon afterward, when Liu Yi was attacked, he was recalled as General Who Pacifies the North and joined the campaign. After the revolt was crushed, Gaozu sent Zhu Lingshi at the head of the main army against Shu and ordered Xi to lead a flanking force down the Zhong River, retaining his rank while also governing Jianping and Badong. The Shu ruler Qiao Zong sent the general Qiao Fuzhi with more than ten thousand men to hold Niupi and Qiao Xiaogou with a large force to block the Dani pass. Xi reached Niupi, routed Fuzhi in battle, pursued him, and cut off his head. When Xiaogou heard that Fuzhi was dead, his army broke and fled. After Chengdu fell, Xi fell ill. In the ninth year of Yixi he died at Niupi in Shu commandery, aged thirty-nine. He was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
3
質年始出三十，屢居名郡，涉獵史籍，尺牘便敏，既有氣幹，好言兵權。 太祖謂可大任，欲以為益州事，未行，徵為使持節、都督徐、兗二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、徐、兗二州刺史。 在鎮奢費，爵命無章，為有司所糾，遇赦。 與范曄、徐湛之等厚善，曄謀反，量質必與之同，會事發，復為建威將軍、義興太守。 元嘉二十六年，太祖謁京陵，質朝丹徒，與何勗、檀和之竝功臣子，時共上禮。 太祖設燕盡歡，賜布千匹。
Zhi was barely past thirty. He had held several prestigious prefectures, read widely in history, wrote with ease, possessed force of character, and loved to talk of military strategy. Emperor Taizu judged him capable of high office and intended to put him in charge of Yi province, but before that could happen he was summoned as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Xu and Yan, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Inspector of both provinces. In office he lived extravagantly and handed out titles without proper authority; the authorities impeached him, but he was pardoned. He was intimate with Fan Ye, Xu Tanzhi, and others. When Ye's conspiracy was uncovered, many assumed Zhi would have joined him; instead he was reappointed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Yixing. In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, when Taizu visited the imperial tombs, Zhi attended at Dantu. He and He Qian, Tan Hezhi, and other sons of founding ministers presented tribute together. Taizu held a feast at which all rejoiced and gave him a thousand bolts of cloth.
4
二十七年春，遷南譙王義宣司馬、寧朔將軍、南平內史。 未之職，會索虜大帥拓跋燾圍汝南，汝南戍主陳憲固守告急。 太祖遣質輕往壽陽，即統彼軍，與安蠻司馬劉康祖等救憲。 虜退走，因使質伐汝南西境刀壁等山蠻，大破之，獲萬餘口，遷太子左衛率。 坐前伐蠻，枉殺隊主嚴祖，又納面首生口，不以送臺，免官。 是時上大舉北討，質白衣與驃騎司馬王方回等率軍出許、洛，安北司馬王玄謨攻滑臺，不拔，質請乘驛代將，太祖不許。
In the spring of the twenty-seventh year he was made Chief Administrator to Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao, General Who Pacifies the North, and Interior Minister of Nanping. Before he could take up the post, the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao besieged Runan. Garrison commander Chen Xian held out and sent an urgent appeal for help. Taizu sent Zhi quickly to Shouyang to take command of the local army and, with Liu Kangzu, Pacifying the Barbarians staff officer, and others, march to relieve Xian. The enemy withdrew, and Zhi was then sent against the mountain tribes of Daobi and neighboring districts on Runan's western marches. He routed them and took more than ten thousand captives, then was promoted to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard. He was dismissed because during the barbarian campaign he had unjustly executed platoon chief Yan Zu and had kept male favorites and captives for himself instead of sending them to the capital. The court then launched a major northern campaign. Though out of office, Zhi joined Flying Cavalry staff officer Wang Fanghui and others in leading troops toward Xu and Luoyang. Pacifying the North staff officer Wang Xuanmo attacked Huatai without success. Zhi asked to ride post relays and replace the commander, but Taizu refused.
5
虜侵徐、豫，拓跋燾率大眾數十萬遂向彭城，以質為輔國將軍、假節、置佐，率萬人北救。 始至盱眙，燾已過淮，冗從僕射胡崇之領質府司馬，崇之副太子積弩將軍毛熙祚亦受統於質。 盱眙城東有高山，質慮虜據之，使崇之、澄之二軍營於山上，質營城南。 虜攻崇之、澄之二營，崇之等力戰不敵，眾散，並為虜所殺。 虜又攻熙祚，熙祚所領悉北府精兵，幢主李灌率厲將士，殺賊甚多。 隊主周胤之、外監楊方生又率射賊，賊垂退，會熙祚被創死，軍遂散亂。 其日質案兵不敢救，故二營一時覆沒。
When the enemy invaded Xu and Yu, Tuoba Tao marched on Pengcheng with several hundred thousand men. Zhi was made General Who Assists the State, given provisional credentials and a staff, and sent north with ten thousand men to relieve the city. Zhi had only just reached Xuyi when Tao had already crossed the Huai. Supernumerary Attendant Hu Chongzhi served as his chief of staff, and Chongzhi's deputy, the crown prince's Repeated Crossbows General Mao Xizuo, was also placed under Zhi's command. A high hill lay east of Xuyi. Fearing the enemy would seize it, Zhi posted Chongzhi's and Cheng's armies on the summit while he camped south of the city. The enemy attacked Chongzhi's and Cheng's camps. They fought hard but were overwhelmed; their troops broke, and all were slain. The enemy then attacked Xizuo, whose troops were all elite Northern Headquarters soldiers. Banner chief Li Guan roused his men to fierce fighting and killed many of the foe. Platoon chief Zhou Yinzhi and outer inspector Yang Fangsheng also led archers against the foe. The enemy was nearly in retreat when Xizuo was wounded and died, and the army collapsed. That day Zhi held his main force back and dared not intervene, so both camps were overrun at once.
6
初，仇池之平也，以崇之為龍驤將軍、北秦州刺史，宋百頃，行至濁水，為索虜所克，舉軍敗散； 崇之及將佐以下，皆為虜所執，後得叛還，至是又為虜所敗焉。 熙祚，司州刺史脩之兄子也。 崇之、熙祚並贈正員郎； 澄之事在祖父燾傳。
Earlier, after the pacification of Qiu Chi, Chongzhi had been made Dragon Cavalry General and Inspector of Northern Qin, with a grant of a hundred qing of land. Marching to Zhuoshui, he was defeated by the Northern Wei and his whole army scattered; Chongzhi and his officers were all taken prisoner, later escaped, and now were defeated again. Xizuo was a nephew of Inspector Xiu of Si province. Chongzhi and Xizuo were both posthumously honored as Regular Gentlemen; Cheng's story is told in the biography of his grandfather Tao.
7
三營既敗，其夕質軍亦奔散，棄輜重器甲，單七百人投盱眙。 盱眙太守沈璞完為守戰之備，城內有實力三千，質大喜，因共守。 虜初南出，後無資糧，唯以百姓為命。 及過淮，食平越、石鱉二屯穀，至是抄掠無所，人馬饑困，聞盱眙有積粟，欲以為歸路之資。 既破崇之等，一攻城不拔，便引眾南向。 城內增修守備，莫不完嚴。 二十八年正月初，燾自廣陵北返，便悉力攻盱眙，就質求酒，質封溲便與之。 燾怒甚，築長圍，一夜便合，開攻道，趣城東北，運東山土石填之。 虜又恐城內水路遁走，乃引大船，欲於君山作浮橋，以絕淮道。 城內乘艦逆戰，大破之。 明旦，賊更方舫為桁，桁上各嚴兵自衛。 城內更擊不能禁，遂於軍山立桁，水陸路竝斷。
After the three camps fell, Zhi's army broke that same evening. He abandoned baggage, heavy gear, and armor and entered Xuyi with only seven hundred men. Xuyi administrator Shen Pu had made thorough preparations for a siege. Three thousand able fighters remained in the city. Zhi was greatly relieved and joined him in the defense. When the invaders first marched south they had no rear supply base and lived off the countryside. After crossing the Huai they consumed the grain stored at Pingyue and Shibie. Now there was nothing left to plunder; men and horses were starving. Hearing that Xuyi held grain, they meant to seize it for the march home. After defeating Chongzhi they assaulted the city once without success and then marched south with their main force. Inside the city the defenders strengthened every part of the fortifications until nothing was left wanting. On the first day of the first month of the twenty-eighth year Tao turned back from Guangling and threw his full strength against Xuyi. He asked Zhi for wine; Zhi sent him a jar of urine instead. Enraged, Tao threw a tight siege ring around the city in a single night, opened assault trenches toward the northeast, and hauled earth and stone from East Hill to fill them. Fearing a breakout by water, they brought up large ships to build a pontoon bridge at Jun Hill and cut the Huai route. The defenders sailed out to meet them and won a great victory on the water. At dawn the next day they lashed boats into rafts, each raft crowded with armed men. The defenders attacked again but could not stop them. The enemy then anchored rafts at Jun Hill and cut off both land and water routes.
8
燾與質書曰：「吾今所遣鬥兵，盡非我國人，城東北是丁零與胡，南是三秦氐、羌。 設使丁零死者，正可減常山、趙郡賊； 胡死，正減并州賊； 氐、羌死，正減關中賊。 卿若殺丁零、胡，無不利。 」質答書曰：「省示，具悉姦懷。 爾自恃四腳，屢犯國疆，諸如此事，不可具說。 王玄謨退于東，梁坦散於西，爾謂何以？ 不聞童謠言邪：『虜馬飲江水，佛狸死卯年。 』此期未至，以二軍開飲江之徑爾，冥期使然，非復人事。 寡人受命相滅，期之白登，師行未遠，爾自送死，豈容復令生全，饗有桑乾哉！ 但爾往攻此城，假令寡人不能殺爾，爾由我而死。 爾若有幸，得為亂兵所殺。 爾若不幸，則生相剿縛，載以一驢，直送都市。 我本不圖全，若天地無靈，力屈於爾，齏之粉之，屠之裂之，如此未足謝本朝。 爾識智及眾力，豈能勝苻堅邪！ 頃年展爾陸梁者，是爾未飲江，太歲未卯年故爾。 斛蘭昔深入彭城，值少日雨，隻馬不返，爾豈憶邪？ 即時春雨已降，四方大眾，始就雲集，爾但安意攻城莫走。 糧食闕乏者告之，當出廩相飴。 得所送劍刀，欲令我揮之爾身邪！ 甚苦，人附反，各自努力，無煩多云。 」是時虜中童謠曰：「軺車北來如穿雉，不意虜馬飲江水。 虜主北歸石濟死，虜欲渡江天不徙。 」故質答引之。 燾大怒，乃作鐵床，於其上施鐵鑱，云破城得質，當坐之此上。 質又與虜眾書曰：「示詔虜中諸士庶：狸伐見與書如別，等正朔之民，何為力自取如此。 大丈夫豈可不知轉禍為福邪！ 今寫臺格如別書，自思之。 」時購斬燾封開國縣侯，食邑一萬戶，賜布絹各萬匹。
Tao wrote to Zhi: "The assault troops I have sent are not my own people at all. Northeast of your city are Dingling and Hu; to the south are Di and Qiang from the Three Qins." "If the Dingling die, that only thins the rebels of Changshan and Zhao; if the Hu die, that only thins the rebels of Bing province; if the Di and Qiang die, that only thins the rebels of Guanzhong. If you kill Dingling and Hu, you lose nothing." Zhi replied: "I have read your letter and understand your treacherous intent perfectly. You trust your four-legged beasts and have raided our borders again and again—too many times to list. Wang Xuanmo retreated in the east and Liang Tan was routed in the west—what do you make of that? Have you not heard the children's rhyme? 'The barbarian horses will drink the river; the Buddha-devil dies in a mao year.' That day has not yet come. Your two armies merely opened the way for the horses to drink—destiny, not human planning. Heaven has charged me to destroy you. I marked Baideng as the day of your fall. Our army has barely marched, yet you rush to your death—do you think I will let you live to feast by the Sanggan? Go on and attack this city. Even if I cannot kill you with my own hand, you will still die by my doing. If you are lucky, you will die in the confusion of battle. If you are unlucky, you will be taken alive, bound, loaded on a donkey, and sent straight to the execution ground. I never expected to come through unscathed. If Heaven fails me and I fall to you, grinding you to powder and cutting you to pieces would still not repay what I owe the dynasty. Do you think your wits and numbers can surpass Fu Jian? The reason you have run wild these past years is simply that you had not yet drunk the river and the mao year had not yet come. Remember Hulan's deep thrust into Pengcheng? After a few days of rain not one horse came back—have you forgotten? The spring rains have already begun. Armies from every quarter are gathering like clouds. Settle down and keep attacking—do not run. If you run short of grain, say so—I will open the granaries and feed you. I have your gift of swords and blades—do you want me to use them on you? Your men have suffered enough. Turn back, each of you, and save yourselves—no need for more words." At that time a rhyme in the enemy camp ran: "The light carriage comes north like shooting a pheasant—who thought the barbarian horses would drink the river?" "The barbarian lord turns north and dies at Shiji; they wish to cross the river but Heaven will not let them." Zhi quoted it in his reply for that reason. Tao was furious. He had an iron bed fitted with iron spikes made, vowing that when the city fell and Zhi was taken, Zhi would be seated upon it. Zhi also wrote to the enemy ranks: "To all officers and commoners in the barbarian host: the fox-devil's letter to me is enclosed. You are subjects of the true calendar—why throw yourselves into such ruin? Surely a true man knows how to turn disaster into advantage! I enclose the court's terms as in the attached letter—judge for yourselves." A bounty was then posted for Tao's head: enfeoffment as marquis of a founding county with ten thousand households, plus ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.
9
虜以鉤車鉤垣樓，城內繋以驅絙，數百人叫喚引之，車不能退。 既夜，以木桶盛人，懸出城外，截其鉤獲之。 明日，又以衝車攻城，城土堅密，每至，頹落不過數升。 虜乃肉薄登城，分番相代，墜而復升，莫有退者，殺傷萬計，虜死者與城平。 又射殺高梁王。 如此三旬，死者過半。 燾聞彭城斷其歸路，京邑遣水軍自海入淮，且疾疫死者甚眾。 二月二日，乃解圍遁走。 上嘉質功，以為使持節、監雍、梁、南、北秦四州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，封開國子，食邑五百戶。 明年，太祖又北伐，使質率所統見力向潼關，質頓兵近郊，不肯時發，獨遣司馬柳元景屯兵境上，不時進軍。 質又顧戀嬖妾，棄營單馬還城，散用臺庫見錢六七百萬，為有司所糾，上不問也。
The enemy used hook-wagons to seize the parapet tower. Inside the city defenders hitched towing ropes; several hundred men hauled and shouted, and the wagons could not be pulled away. That night men were lowered outside the wall in wooden tubs, cut off the hooks, and brought them back. The next day they attacked again with battering rams. The wall earth was firm and dense; each blow brought down only a few handfuls of soil. The enemy pressed in close under the walls and swarmed up in relays, falling and climbing again without retreat. Tens of thousands were killed or wounded, and enemy corpses heaped as high as the ramparts. The defenders also shot dead the Prince of Gaoliang. After thirty days of such fighting, more than half the attackers were dead. Tuoba Tao learned that Pengcheng had blocked his retreat, that a fleet from the capital was entering the Huai from the sea, and that disease was killing great numbers of his men. On the second day of the second month he broke off the siege and withdrew. Emperor Taizu praised Zhi's achievement and made him Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong, Liang, and the Southern and Northern Qin provinces, General Who Wins the Day, Pacifying the Barbarians Commandant, and Inspector of Yong, creating him Viscount of a Founding State with five hundred households. The following year Taizu mounted another northern expedition and ordered Zhi to march his available troops toward Tong Pass. Zhi camped in the suburbs and would not move on schedule, sending only Liu Yuanjing to hold the frontier without pressing the advance. Zhi again lingered over a favorite concubine, left camp alone on horseback for the city, and spent six or seven million in cash from the imperial treasury. Though the authorities impeached him, the emperor took no action.
10
元兇弑立，以質為丹陽尹，加征虜將軍。 質家遣門生師顗報質，具太祖崩問。 質疏顗所言，馳告司空義宣，又遣州祭酒從事田穎起銜命報世祖，率眾五千，馳下討逆，自陽口進江陵義宣。 質諸子在都邑，聞質舉義，並逃亡。 劭欲相慰悅，乃下書曰：「臧敦等無因自駭，急便竄逸，迷昧過甚，良可怪歎。 質國戚勳臣，忠誠篤亮，方當顯位，贊翼京輦，而子弟波迸，傷其乃懷。 可遣宣譬令還，咸復本位。 」劭尋錄得敦，使大將軍義恭行訓杖三十，厚給賜之。 義宣得質報，即日舉兵，馳信報世祖，板進質號征北將軍。 質逕赴尋陽，與世祖同下。
After Liu Shao murdered his way to the throne, he made Zang Zhi Governor of Danyang and promoted him to General Who Captures Barbarians. Zhi's family sent his student retainer Shi Yan to inform him with full details of Taizu's death. Zhi wrote out Yan's report, sent word in haste to Prince Yixuan, Minister of Works, and dispatched Tian Yingqi, provincial libationer, with orders to notify Emperor Xiaowu. Leading five thousand men downstream against the usurpers, he advanced from Yangkou to Jiangling to join Prince Yixuan. Zhi's sons in the capital, learning that he had taken up arms against the usurpers, all fled. Liu Shao tried to reassure him and issued an edict: "Zang Dun and the others panicked without reason and fled at once—their folly is excessive and truly lamentable. Zang Zhi is a royal kinsman and founding minister, loyal and steadfast, soon to hold high office at court; that his sons fled in panic must wound his heart. Send word to explain matters and call them back; they shall all resume their former posts. " Liu Shao soon found Dun, had Grand General Yigong give him thirty strokes of discipline, and rewarded him generously. When Prince Yixuan received Zhi's message, he rose in arms that same day, sent word to Emperor Xiaowu, and provisionally promoted Zhi to General Who Campaigns North. Zhi went directly to Xunyang and sailed downstream with Emperor Xiaowu.
11
世祖至新亭即位，以質為都督江州諸軍事、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史，加散騎常侍，持節如故。 使質率所領自白下步上，直至廣莫門，門者不守。 薛安都、程天祚等亦自南掖門入，與質同會太極殿，生禽元兇。 仍使質留守朝堂，甲仗百人自防。 封始興郡公，食邑三千戶。 之鎮，舫千餘乘，部伍前後百餘里，六平乘竝施龍子幡。
At Xinting Emperor Xiaowu took the throne and made Zhi commander of Jiang province, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with Three Excellencies status and an opened office, Inspector of Jiang, Regular Attendant, and Bearer of the Staff as before. He sent Zhi to lead his men on foot from Baixia up to Guangmo Gate, which the guards did not hold. Xue Andu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others entered through the Southern Flank Gate, joined Zhi in the Hall of Supreme Pole, and took Liu Shao alive. He left Zhi to hold the audience hall, with a hundred armed men for his own guard. Zhi was created Duke of Shixing with a fief of three thousand households. When he went to his post he traveled in more than a thousand boats, his train stretching over a hundred li, with dragon-prince banners on six covered barges.
12
時世祖自攬威柄，而質以少主遇之，是事專行，多所求欲。 及至尋陽，刑政慶賞，不復諮稟朝廷。 盆口、鉤圻米，輒散用之，臺符屢加檢詰，質漸猜懼。 自謂人才足為一世英傑，始聞國禍，便有異圖，以義宣凡闇，易可制勒，欲外相推奉，以成其志。 及至江陵，便致拜稱名。 質於義宣雖為兄弟，而年大近十歲，義宣驚曰：「君何意拜弟？ 」質曰：「事中宜然。 」時義宣已推崇世祖，故其計不行。 質每慮事泄，及至新亭，又拜江夏王義恭，義恭愕然，問質所以。 質曰：「天下屯危，禮異常日，前在荊州，亦拜司空。 」會義宣有憾於世祖，事在義宣傳。 質因此密信說誘，陳朝廷得失。 又謂：「震主之威，不可持久，主相勢均，事不兩立。 今專據閫外，地勝兵強，持疑不決，則後機致禍。 」質女為義宣子采妻，謂質無復異同，納其說。 且義宣腹心將佐蔡超民之徒，咸有富貴之情，願義宣得，欲倚質威名，以成其業，又勸獎義宣。 義宣時未受丞相，質子敦為黃門侍郎，奉詔敦勸，道經尋陽，質令敦具更譬說，并言世祖短長，義宣乃意定。 馳報豫州刺史魯爽，期孝建元年秋同舉。 爽失旨，即便起兵。 遣人至京邑報弟瑜，瑜席捲奔叛。 瑜弟弘為質府佐，世祖遣報質，質於是執臺使，狼狽舉兵。 上表曰：
Emperor Xiaowu was then tightening his grip on power, but Zhi treated him as a junior sovereign, doing as he pleased and demanding much. Once at Xunyang he no longer consulted the court on punishments, policy, or rewards. He kept spending the grain stored at Pankou and Gouqi as he saw fit; repeated imperial rebukes made Zhi increasingly wary and afraid. He thought himself a match for any man of the age and had other plans from the moment he heard of the coup. Judging Prince Yixuan dull and easy to manage, he meant to use him as a figurehead while pursuing his own aims. On reaching Jiangling he bowed to Prince Yixuan and addressed him by personal name. Though Zhi and Prince Yixuan were sworn brothers, Zhi was nearly ten years older. Prince Yixuan was astonished: "Why do you bow to your younger brother? " Zhi replied: "These circumstances call for it. " But Prince Yixuan was already deferring to Emperor Xiaowu, so the scheme failed. Zhi always feared exposure; at Xinting he bowed again to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, who was startled and asked why. Zhi said: "The realm is in crisis and ceremony is not what it was in normal times. In Jing province I bowed to the Minister of Works as well. " It happened that Prince Yixuan already resented Emperor Xiaowu; the details are in his biography. Zhi then wrote secretly to win him over, laying out what the court had done wrong and right. He also argued: "Power that overshadows the throne cannot endure; when ruler and minister are equals, one of them must fall. You now hold the provinces beyond the capital with strong ground and troops; if you hesitate, you will lose your chance and bring ruin on yourself. " Zhi's daughter was married to Prince Yixuan's son Cai; believing Zhi had no further reservations, Prince Yixuan accepted the plan. Prince Yixuan's inner circle, men like Cai Chaomin, all hungered for rank and riches, wanted him to prevail, hoped to ride on Zhi's name and power, and pressed him further. Prince Yixuan had not yet been made Chancellor. Zhi's son Dun, an Attendant of the Yellow Gate, was sent with an edict of persuasion; passing Xunyang, Zhi had Dun repeat the whole case and discuss Emperor Xiaowu's strengths and failings, and Prince Yixuan made up his mind. He sent word in haste to Lu Shuang, Inspector of Yu, fixing the autumn of the first year of Xiaojian for a joint rising. Lu Shuang had fallen from favor and rose in arms at once. He sent a messenger to the capital to warn his brother Yu, who packed up and fled to join the revolt. Yu's younger brother Hong served on Zhi's staff. When Emperor Xiaowu sent word to Zhi, Zhi seized the imperial messenger and rose in arms in disarray. He memorialized the throne as follows:
13
臣聞執藥隨親，非情謬於甘苦； 揮斤斬毒，豈忘痛於肌膚。 蓋以先疑後順，忠焉必往； 忍小存大，雖愛必從。 丞相臣義宣，育哲台鉉，拊聲聯服，定主勤王之業，勳越乎齊、晉； 宗戚懿親之寄，望崇於魯、衛。 而惡直醜正，實繁有黨，或染凶作偽，疾害元功； 或藉勞挾寵，乘威縱戾。 自知愆深釁重，必貽剿戮，乃成紫毀朱，交間忠輔。 崇樹私徒，招聚群惡，念舊愛老，無一而存，豈不由凶醜相扇，志肆讒惑。 陛下垂慈狎達，不稍惟疑，遂令負扆席圖，蔽於流議，投杼市虎，成於十夫。 鑒古揆今，實懷危逼，故投袂樊、葉，立節於本朝； 揮戈晉陽，務清於君側。 臣誠庸懦，奉教前朝，雖恧《緇衣》好賢之美，敢希《巷伯》惡惡之情，固已藉風聽而宵憤，撫短策而馳念。 況乃宏命爰格，誠係宗社，今奉旨前邁，星言啟行。
I have heard that one who holds out medicine for a parent does not mistake bitterness for sweetness in feeling; and one who swings the axe to cut out poison does not forget the pain to flesh and skin. This is because loyalty, once doubt is resolved, must act; and because one must endure a lesser hurt to save the greater good, even at the cost of what one loves. Chancellor Prince Yixuan, raised in wisdom at court, whose fame binds the realm, who fixed and led the cause of saving the dynasty, with merit surpassing the states of Qi and Jin; entrusted as a royal kinsman of the highest standing, his prestige rivaling the ancient domains of Lu and Wei. Yet those who hate the upright and revile the good are many and faction-ridden; some stained with evil and deceit who injure the founding ministers; others trading on past service and court favor, abusing power and acting with impunity. Knowing their guilt is grave and fearing extermination, they invert black and white and set loyal ministers against one another. They build private factions and gather villains; those who remembered the old and honored the aged—none survive. Is this not because the wicked inflame one another and give free rein to slander? Your Majesty's kindness and easy trust left no room for doubt, so the ruler at the screen is blinded by rumor—like the tale of the shuttle cast away and the market tiger, made real by ten men's words. Weighing past and present, I feel true urgency; therefore I have thrown off my robe as at Fan and Ye and taken my stand for this dynasty; and raised arms at Jinyang to purge evil from the ruler's side. Your servant is indeed dull and timid, trained under the former court; though I fall short of the praise for loving worthies in Black Robes, I dare hope for the Lane Count's hatred of evil, and have long burned with nightly anger and urgent resolve. Moreover the great mandate has now arrived and truly binds the altars of state; obeying orders I advance and set out at once.
14
臣本凡瑣，少無遠概，因緣際會，遂班槐鼎，素望既盈，愜心實足，豈應徼功非冀，更希異寵，直以蔓草難除，去惡宜速，是以無顧夷險，慮不及身。 仰恃天眷，察亮丹款，苟血誠不照，甘心罪戮。
I am by nature petty and without great vision; by chance I rose to ministerial rank, my lifelong wishes fulfilled and my heart content. I seek no unearned glory or further extraordinary favor—only because weeds are hard to uproot and evil must be cut down quickly, I take no account of hardship or even of my own life. Trusting in Heaven's grace, I pray you will see my loyal heart; if my devotion is not recognized, I accept punishment willingly.
15
伏願陛下先鑒元輔匪躬茂節，末錄庸瑣奉國微誠，不遂淟涊之情，以失四海之望，昭戮馬劍，顯肆市朝，則結旌向國，全鋒凱歸，九流凝序，三光並耀，斯則仰說宗廟，俯愜兆民。 裁表感慨，涕言無已。
I humbly pray that Your Majesty will first recognize the Chancellor's selfless excellence and then note this humble servant's small loyalty to the state; do not give way to weakness and forfeit the hope of the realm. Let the guilty be punished openly in the market and at court—then banners will turn homeward, blades intact, victory won; all orders will settle, heaven's lights shine together, the ancestral temple rejoice above, and the people be satisfied below. Thus I close this memorial in grief, my tearful words endless.
16
加魯弘輔國將軍，下戍大雷。 馳報義宣，義宣遣諮議參軍劉諶之萬人就弘。 世祖遣撫軍將軍柳元景統豫州刺史王玄謨等水軍，屯梁山洲內，兩岸築偃月壘，水陸待之。 殿中將軍沈靈賜領百舸，破其前軍於南陵，生禽軍主徐慶安、軍副王僧，質至梁山，亦夾陣兩岸。 元景檄書宣告曰：
Zhi promoted Lu Hong to General Who Assists the State and posted him to garrison Dalei. He sent word in haste to Prince Yixuan, who dispatched Senior Adviser Liu Chenzhi with ten thousand men to reinforce Hong. Emperor Xiaowu sent Liu Yuanjing, Pacification Army General, to command the fleet of Wang Xuanmo, Inspector of Yu, and others. They encamped on the Liangshan sandbar, built crescent ramparts on both banks, and waited by land and water. Palace Guard General Shen Lingci led a hundred boats, routed their vanguard at Nanling, and took alive Xu Qing'an, army commander, and Wang Seng, his deputy. When Zhi reached Liangshan he too drew up battle lines on both banks. Liu Yuanjing's public proclamation read:
17
夫革道應運，基命之洪符； 嗣業興邦，紹歷之明筭。 自非瑞積神衷，德充民極，孰能升臨寶位，景屬天居。 大宋啟期，理高中世，皇根帝葉，永流無疆。 夷陂遞來，遘茲凶難，國禍冤深，人綱鬱滅。 主上聖略聰武，孝感通神，義變草木，哀動精緯，躬幸南郢，親掃大逆，道援橫流，德模靈造，三光重照，七廟載興。
To change the Way in accord with destiny is the great sign of a founding mandate; to inherit the enterprise and raise the state is the clear design of continuing the dynastic line. Unless omens gather in the sacred heart and virtue fills the summit of the people, who could ascend the throne and take heaven's seat? Great Song opens its age, its principle lofty among middle kingdoms, its imperial root and royal line flowing on without end. Disaster followed disaster until this villainous crisis struck; the state's wrongs ran deep and the bonds of humanity were choked off. Our sovereign's wisdom is keen and martial, his filial devotion moves heaven, his righteousness touches even grass and trees, his grief stirs the celestial signs. He went in person to Southern Ying, swept away great treason himself, rescued the realm from flood, modeled virtue on creation itself, restored the three lights, and raised the seven temples anew.
18
臧質少負疵釁，衣冠不齒，昧利誣天，著於觸事。 受任述職，不以宣效為心； 專方蒞民，惟以侵剝為務。 官自賄至，族以貨傾。 是以康周陀覆命屠宗，冤達蒼昊； 郭伯、西門遺出自皁隸，寵越州朝。 往蒞東守，鬻爵三千。 率卒西討，竊俘取黜。 荷恩彭、泗，貪虐以逞，坑戮邊氓，忽若草芥，傾渴倉庾，割沒軍糧。 作牧漢南，公盜府蓄，矯易文簿，專行欺妄。 及受命北伐，憚役緩期，師出有辰，顧懷私愛，匹馬棄眾，宵行獨返，遂復攜嬪擁姬，淫宴軍幕。 孔、范之變，顯於逆辭。 凡此諸釁，皆彰著於憲簡，振曝於觀聽。
Zang Zhi has carried stains since youth; gentlemen will not rank him with them. He deceives Heaven for gain, and every act shows it. Given office and charged with duty, he has never had spreading benefit as his aim; holding a province and ruling the people, he has made plunder his only business. He bought office with bribes and toppled his clan with greed. Thus Kang Zhoutuo was killed and his clan wiped out, his wrongs reaching to heaven itself; Guo Bo and Ximen Yi rose from menial ranks yet enjoyed favor beyond what the provincial court allowed. When he governed in the east he sold off three thousand official posts. Leading troops on the western expedition, he privately kept captives and evaded proper accounting. Favored at Peng and Si, he gave free rein to greed and cruelty, slaughtered frontier people as if they were weeds, emptied the granaries, and seized army rations. As governor south of the Han he openly looted the treasury, falsified the registers, and ruled by fraud alone. Ordered on the northern campaign, he shrank from the hardship and delayed; though the army had a fixed day to march, he turned to private affairs, abandoned his troops on a single horse, returned alone by night, and then brought concubines into camp for debauchery in the command tent. His part in the Kong and Fan affair shows plainly in his treasonous language. All these crimes are recorded in the law and exposed before every eye and ear.
19
去歲義舉，雖豫誠款，而淹留西楚，私相崇戴，奉書致命，形於心跡。 新亭之捷，大難已夷，凶命假存，懸在晷刻，廣莫之軍，曾無遺矢，重關自開，偽眾已潰，質猶復盤桓衢巷，後騎陳師。 勞不足甄，定於朝議，而虛張功伐，扇動怨辭，自謂斯舉，勳莫己若。 初踐殿守，忘犬馬之情，奔趣帑藏，頓傾天府。 山海弘量，苞荒藏疾，錄其一介之心，掩其不逞之釁。 遂爵首元等，職班盛級，優榮溢寵，莫與為疇。 自恣醜薄，罔知涯涘，干謁陳聞，曾無紀極，請樂窮太子之英，求器盡官府之選。 徐司空匪躬王室，遭罹凶禍，質與之少長，親交兼常，曾無撫孤之仁，惟聞陵侮之酷，尺田寸寶，靡有孑遺。 及受命南徂，臨路滋甚，逼奪妻嬪，略市金帛，怨動京邑，醜聞都鄙。 棄逐舊故，委蔑忠勤，魯尚期、尹周之徒，心腹所倚，泣訴於御筵； 袁同、連子敬之疇，爪牙所杖，一逝而不反。 雖上旨頻煩，屢求勞牒，質但稱伐在己，不逮僚隸，託咎朝廷，歸罪有司，國士解心，有識莫附。 何文敬趨走廝養，天性愚狡，質迷其奸諂，寘懷委仗，遂外擅威刑，內遊房室。 質生與釁俱，不可詳究，擢發數罪，曾何足言！
In last year's loyal rising he took part in good faith, yet he lingered in Western Chu, privately honoring another lord, sending letters of allegiance that showed plainly in word and deed. After the victory at Xinting the great crisis was over; the usurper's life hung by a thread. At Guangmo Gate not an arrow was lost, the passes opened of themselves, and the rebel force was already broken—yet Zhi still lingered in the streets with his rear guard drawn up. The court judged his service unworthy of special reward, yet he inflated his achievements, stirred up complaint, and believed no one had done more than he. When first assigned to guard the palace he forgot his duty as a subject, rushed to the treasury, and emptied the imperial storehouse at a stroke. The throne's magnanimity, vast as mountains and seas, embraced his faults and hid his crimes, crediting his smallest show of loyalty and covering his unrestrained offenses. He was given founding merit of the first rank, offices among the highest grades, and honors beyond measure—none could compare. Shameless and base beyond measure, he petitioned the throne without end, demanding the crown prince's best musicians and every fine object in the imperial stores. Minister of Works Xu gave himself wholly to the throne and met a villain's death. Zhi had known him from youth and counted him a close friend, yet showed no mercy to his orphans—only cruel abuse—and left not a field or treasure untouched. Ordered south, his conduct on the road grew worse still: he seized men's wives and concubines, looted markets for gold and silk, and stirred resentment in the capital and scandal in town and country. He cast off old friends and treated loyal service with contempt; Lu Shangqi, Yin Zhou, and others whom he had trusted as his inner circle wept out their grievances at the imperial banquet; men like Yuan Tong and Lian Zijing, the tools he relied on, departed once and never came back. Though the throne sent repeated orders demanding accounts of merit, Zang Zhi kept every victory for himself and gave none to his officers. He blamed the court and pinned failures on the bureaucracy. The realm's best men turned away, and no one worth following would stand with him. He Wenjing had risen from the ranks of runners and stable boys—a man naturally sly and stupid. Zang Zhi, blinded by his smooth tongue, put his whole trust in him. Soon Wenjing wielded punishments in public and wandered the women's quarters in private. Zang Zhi had been guilty from the cradle; no ledger could hold the full account. To number his crimes one by one would still leave the tale unfinished.
20
丞相威重位尊，任居分陝，宗國倚賴，實兼恆情，而不及謙沖之塗，弗見逆順之訓，蔽同郤至，理乖范燮。 遂乃遠忽世祀，近受欺構，杖納奸疏，還謀社稷。 日者宴安上流，坐觀成敗，示遣疲卒，眾裁三千，戎馬不供，軍糧靡獻。 皇朝直以親秩之重，酬寵兼極，近漸別子，禮越常均，苟識無所守，功弗由己，必為義不全，終於敗德。 今茲放命，恨心於本，推諸昔歲，跡是誠非矣。 且家國夷險，情事異常，豫是臣子，孰不星赴，而玩寇忘哀，曾無奔拽。 面蕃十稔，惠政蔑聞，重贓深掠，縱欲已甚，姬妾百房，尼僧千計，敗道傷俗，悖亂人神，民怨盈塗，國謗彌歲。 又賊劭未禽，凶威猶強，將毀其私墳，戮其諸子，圖成駭機，垂賴義舉，捷期雲速，不日告平，釋怨毒之心，解倒懸之急，論恩敘德，造育為重。 援人自助，棄人快讒，怙亂疑功，未聞其比。
As Grand Counselor he held awesome rank and ruled half the empire; the dynasty leaned on him, as was only natural. Yet he never learned humility, never took to heart the difference between loyalty and treason. He shut his eyes like Xi Zhi of old and turned his back on the justice Fan Xie had stood for. He scorned the rites owed to distant emperors while swallowing the lies whispered at his elbow. He embraced traitors' petitions and set his sights on the throne itself. Of late he had banqueted in comfort upstream, watching the war as a spectator. He sent out a token force of three thousand worn-out men, furnished no horses, and sent no grain. The court had heaped honor on him for the sake of blood ties alone. Lately he had begun favoring a younger son beyond what custom allowed. When a man holds no fixed loyalty and claims victories he did not earn, his righteousness cannot stand—and his virtue rots away. Today's rebellion grew from old bitterness at the core. Look back a few years and the wrong turn was already plain. When the throne and the realm are in danger, every loyal subject should fly to the rescue like a falling star. Instead he toyed with the rebels and forgot his grief, never once hurrying to help. Ten years he ruled his domain, and not one act of mercy was ever reported. He taxed and robbed without restraint, indulged every appetite—a hundred rooms of concubines, a thousand nuns in his train. He defiled the faith, poisoned custom, and turned heaven and earth upside down. The people's anger choked the roads; scandal about him filled every year. Liu Shao the usurper was still at large, his terror still strong. They meant to raze Zang Zhi's family tombs and kill his sons. At that dreadful hour the realm hung on righteous arms; victory would come swift as storm clouds, peace within days. Then poisonous hatred could be laid down and the nation lifted from its peril. When grace is weighed, the gift of life counts above all. To use allies only to save himself, to cast them aside and feast on their ruin, to lean on rebellion yet doubt every deed of loyalty—nothing like it had ever been heard.
21
僕以不肖，過蒙榮私，荷佩升越，光絕倫伍。 家本北邊，志存慷慨，常甘投生，以殉艱棘，惟恩思難，激氣衝襟，故以眺三湘而永慨，望九江而遐憤。 若使身死國康，誓在殞命，況仰稟聖略，俯鞠義徒，萬全之形，愚夫所照。 夫薛竟陵控率突騎，陸道步馳。 檀右衛、申右率、垣游擊整勒銳師，飛輪構路。 王豫州方舟繕甲，久已前驅。 僕訓卒利兵，淩波電進。 沈鎮軍、蕭安南接舳連旌，首尾風合。 驃騎竟陵王懿親令譽，問望攸歸，大司馬江夏王道略明遠，徽猷茂世，並旄鉞臨塗，雲驅齊引。 群兵競邁，秘駕徐啟。 八鑾搖響，五牛舒斾。 千乘雷動，萬舳雲回。 騰威發號，星流漢轉。 以上臨下，易於轉圓。 加以三謀協從，七緯告慶，幽顯同心，昭然易睹。
I am a lesser man who has received far more private favor than I deserve. The rank I bear outshines every man around me. My house comes from the northern marches, and my heart burns with old frontier courage. I have always been ready to die in hard service. Thinking on the throne's grace and the realm's peril, wrath fills my chest—when I look toward the Three Xiang I am seized by lasting grief, and when I gaze on the Nine Rivers my anger runs far. If my death would restore the realm, I swear to lay down my life. And now, with the emperor's strategy above me and righteous soldiers below, even a fool can see how victory will come. Xue of Jingling leads shock cavalry that thunder overland. Tan of the Right Guard, Shen Youzhi of the Right Commandant, and Yuan the Strike General have whetted elite troops whose chariots block every road. Wang of Yuzhou, with armored boats lashed bow to stern, has marched in the van for days. I have trained my men and honed their blades; we cross the waves like lightning. Shen the Area Commander and Xiao the Pacifier of the South have linked their fleets, bow to stern and banner to banner, moving as one like a single wind. The Grand General, Prince of Jingling, commands in person, and every eye turns to his fame. The Grand Marshal, Prince of Jiangxia, sees far and bears virtue worthy of the age. Both ride forth under imperial banners, sweeping forward like storm clouds in unison. Armies surge ahead while the emperor's hidden carriage moves slowly into the field. Imperial bells sway and ring; the five-ox chariots unfurl their banners. A thousand chariots roll like thunder; ten thousand hulls wheel like clouds. Their majesty rises, their orders fly; they move like stars streaming across the sky. To strike from above against those below is as easy as turning a wheel. Add to this that counsel is united, the heavens themselves show favor, and the living and the dead stand as one—the outcome is plain for all to see.
22
諸君或世荷恩幸，或身聞教義，當知君臣大節，誓不可犯，冠屨至誨，難用倒設。 履安奉順，聲泰事全，孰與附逆居危，身害名醜，慈親垂白受戮，弱子嬰孩就誅。 所以有詔遲回，未震雷霆者，正為諸君身拘寇手，或懷乃心。 吉凶由人，無謂為遠，今而不變，後悔何及。 授檄之日，心馳賊庭。
Some of you have owed the throne favor for generations; others have heard its teaching with your own ears. You know the bond between sovereign and subject cannot be broken. Cap and shoes are not worn on the wrong feet—and loyalty is not worn inside out. To walk in safety under lawful obedience, with honor intact and life secure—what is that beside clinging to treason, living in peril, ruining yourself and your name, and seeing your gray-haired parents cut down and your infant sons killed? That is why the imperial decree has held back and thunder has not yet fallen—because some of you are still in the rebels' grip, and some still keep loyal hearts. Fortune and ruin lie in your own hands—do not think the choice is distant. If you do not turn now, regret will come too late. From the day this proclamation was issued, my heart has flown toward the rebel camp.
23
義宣亦相次係至。 江夏王與義宣書曰：「昔桓玄借兵於仲堪，有似今日。 」義宣由此與質相疑。 質進計曰：「今以萬人取南州，則梁山中絕，萬人綴玄謨，必不敢動。 質浮舟外江，直向石頭，此上略也。 」義宣將從之，腹心劉諶之曰：「質求前馳，此志難測。 不如盡銳攻梁山，事克然後長驅，萬安之計也。 」質遣將尹周之攻胡子反、柳叔政於西壘，時子反渡東岸就玄謨計事，聞賊至，馳歸。 周之攻壘甚急，劉季之水軍殊死戰，賊勢盛，求救於玄謨。 玄謨不遣，崔勳之固爭，乃遣勳之救之。 比至，城已陷，勳之戰死，季之收眾而退。 子反、叔政奔還東岸，玄謨斬子反軍副李文仲。
Prince Yixuan was captured soon after. The Prince of Jiangxia wrote to Prince Yixuan: "Once Huan Xuan borrowed soldiers from Yin Zhongkan. What is happening now looks much the same." After that letter, Prince Yixuan began to distrust Zang Zhi. Zang Zhi proposed: "Send ten thousand men to take the southern commandery and cut Liangshan in half. Pin Xuannmo with another ten thousand, and he will not dare stir." "I will sail down the outer river straight for Shitou. That is the best plan." Prince Yixuan was ready to agree when his confidant Liu Chenzhi said, "Zang Zhi wants to ride in the van. His purpose is hard to read." "Better to throw every spear at Liangshan. Once it falls, we can march on without fear. That is the safest course." Zang Zhi sent Yin Zhouzhi to attack Hu Zifan and Liu Shuzheng at the western fort. Hu Zifan had crossed to the east bank to confer with Xuannmo; when he heard the enemy was coming, he galloped back. Yin Zhouzhi hammered the fort without pause. Liu Jizhi's fleet fought to the death, but the rebels' strength grew, and they sent to Xuannmo for help. Xuannmo refused to send aid. Cui Xunzhi argued until he was heard, and at last Xuannmo sent Xunzhi to the rescue. By the time he arrived the fort had already fallen. Cui Xunzhi was killed in the fighting, and Liu Jizhi gathered what men he could and retreated. Hu Zifan and Liu Shuzheng fled back to the east bank. Xuannmo had Hu Zifan's deputy Li Wenzhong beheaded.
24
質欲仍攻東城，義宣黨顏樂之說義宣曰：「質若復拔東城，則大功盡歸之矣。 宜遣麾下自行。 」義宣遣劉諶之就質，陳軍城南。 玄謨留羸弱守城，悉精兵出戰，薛安都騎軍前出，垣護之督諸將繼之。 戰良久，賊陣小拔，騎得入。 劉季之、宗越又陷其西北，眾軍乘之，乃大潰。 因風放火，船艦悉見焚燒，延及西岸。 質求義宣欲一計事，密已出走矣。 質不知所為，亦走，眾悉降散。 質至尋陽，焚燒府舍，載妓妾西奔。 使所寵何文敬領兵居前，至西陽。 西陽太守魯方平，質之黨也，至是懷貳，誑文敬曰：「傳詔宣敕，唯捕元惡一人，餘並無所問。 」文敬棄眾而走。
Zang Zhi wanted to press the attack on the eastern city. Yan Lezhi, a follower of Prince Yixuan, warned him: "If Zang Zhi takes the eastern city too, all the glory will be his." "Send your own men to do it instead." Prince Yixuan sent Liu Chenzhi to Zang Zhi, and they drew up their forces south of the city. Xuannmo left the weak to hold the walls and marched out every able man. Xue Andu's cavalry led the charge, with Yuan Huzhi directing the other commanders behind him. The fight dragged on until the rebel line buckled a little and the horsemen broke through. Liu Jizhi and Zong Yue punched through the northwest as well. The whole army surged forward, and the rebels broke completely. They lit fires with the wind at their backs. Every ship went up in flames, and the blaze leaped to the western shore. Zang Zhi went to Prince Yixuan to talk strategy, but the prince had already slipped away in secret. Zang Zhi, at a loss, fled as well. His army surrendered and melted away. Zang Zhi reached Xunyang, torched the yamen, loaded his concubines aboard, and fled west. He sent his favorite He Wenjing ahead with the vanguard as far as Xiyang. Lu Fangping, prefect of Xiyang and once Zang Zhi's ally, now turned doubtful. He lied to He Wenjing: "Imperial orders say only the ringleader is wanted. No one else will be punished." He Wenjing abandoned his men and ran.
25
質先以妹夫羊沖為武昌郡，質往投之。 既至，沖已為郡丞胡庇之所殺。 無所歸，乃入南湖逃竄，無食，摘蓮噉之。 追兵至，窘急，以荷覆頭，自沈於水，出鼻。 軍主鄭俱兒望見，射之中心，兵刃亂至，腸胃纏縈水草，隊主裘應斬質首，傳京都，時年五十五。 錄尚書江夏王臣義恭、左僕射臣宏等奏曰：「臧質底棄下才，而藉遇深重，窮愚悖常，構煽凶逆，變至滔天，志圖泯夏，違恩叛德，罪過恆科。 梟首之憲，有國通典，懲戾思永，去惡宜深。 臣等參議，須辜日限意，使依漢王莽事例，漆其頭首，藏於武庫。 庶為鑒戒，昭示將來。 」詔可。
Zang Zhi had earlier made his brother-in-law Yang Chong prefect of Wuchang, and now he fled to him for shelter. When he arrived, Yang Chong was already dead—killed by the assistant prefect Hu Bizi. With nowhere left to turn, he hid in South Lake. He had nothing to eat and survived on lotus roots he pulled from the mud. When pursuers closed in, he covered his head with a lotus leaf, sank beneath the water, and breathed through his nose alone. The garrison commander Zheng Ju'er spotted him and drove an arrow through his chest. Soldiers closed in from every side; his guts tangled in the weeds. Squad leader Qiu Ying took Zang Zhi's head and sent it to the capital. He was fifty-five. The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, together with Left Vice Director Hong and others, memorialized: "Zang Zhi was a man of little talent who yet received the deepest favor. In blind folly he broke every law, stirred rebellion, and raised a storm that shook heaven. He sought to destroy the dynasty, betrayed the throne's grace, and turned his back on virtue—crimes that call for the harshest penalty." Displaying a traitor's head is the law of every realm. To punish rebellion and warn the ages, evil must be rooted out to the full. We humbly propose that, once the day of execution arrives, his head be lacquered and kept in the armory, following the precedent set for Wang Mang in Han times. Let it stand as a warning for all who come after. The emperor approved.
26
質初下，義宣以質子敦為征虜將軍、雝州刺史。 質留子敞為監軍，將敦自隨，至是竝為武昌郡所執送。 敦官至黃門郎。 敦弟敷，司徒屬。 敷弟敞，太子洗馬。 敞弟斁，敦子仲璋，質之二子二孫未有名，同誅。
When Zang Zhi first sailed downstream, Prince Yixuan made his son Dun General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and inspector of Yong Province. Zang Zhi had left his son Chang as army supervisor and taken Dun with him. Now both were seized in Wuchang and sent under guard to the capital. Dun had risen to Attendant at the Yellow Gate. Dun's younger brother Fu served on the staff of the Ministry of Education. Fu's younger brother Chang was Groom in Attendance to the Heir Apparent. Chang's younger brother Yi, Dun's son Zhongzhang, and two other sons and two grandsons of Zang Zhi too young to bear names were all put to death.
27
質之起兵也，豫章太守任薈之、臨川內史劉懷之、鄱陽太守杜仲儒竝為盡力，發遣郡丁，并送糧運，伏誅。 任薈之，字處茂，樂安人也。 歷世祖、南平王鑠撫軍右軍司馬、長史行事。 太祖稱之曰：「望雖不足，才能有餘。 」杜仲儒，杜驥兄子也。 豫章望蔡子相孫沖之起義拒質，質遣將郭會膚、史山夫討之，為沖之所破。 世祖發詔，以為尚書都官曹郎中。 沖之，太原中都人，晉秘書監盛曾孫也。 官至右軍將軍，巴東太守。 後事在劉琬傳。 沈靈賜以破質前軍於南陵功，封南平縣男，食邑三百戶。 贈崔勳之通直郎。 大司馬參軍劉天賜亦梁山戰亡，追贈給事中。
When Zang Zhi rebelled, Ren Huizhi of Yuzhang, Liu Huaizhi of Linchuan, and Du Zhongru of Poyang all gave him their full support—raising levies and sending grain. All three were executed. Ren Huizhi, styled Chumao, came from Le'an. He had served under Emperor Xiaowu and Prince Shuo of Nanping as Right Army Major and acting chief clerk on the Area Commander's staff. Emperor Taizu once said of him: "His fame may fall short, but his ability more than makes up for it." Du Zhongru was the nephew of Du Ji. Sun Chongzhi of Wangcai in Yuzhang took up arms against Zang Zhi. Zang Zhi sent Guo Huifu and Shi Shanfu against him, and they were beaten. Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict making him a master of writing in the Bureau of Punishments. Chongzhi came from Zhongdu in Taiyuan and was the great-grandson of Sheng, Jin's Director of the Secretariat. He later rose to Right Army General and prefect of Badong. His later career is told in the biography of Liu Wan. For breaking Zang Zhi's vanguard at Nanling, Shen Lingci was made Baron of Nanping with a fief of three hundred households. Cui Xunzhi was posthumously made Attendant Direct. Liu Tianci, aide to the Grand Marshal, also fell at Liangshan and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
28
魯爽，小名女生，扶風郿人也。 祖宗之，字彥仁，晉孝武太元末，自鄉里出襄陽，歷官至南郡太守。 義熙元年起義，襲偽雝州刺史桓蔚，進向江陵。 以功為輔國將軍、雝州刺史，封霄城縣侯，食邑千五百戶。 桓謙、荀林逼江陵，宗之率眾馳赴，事在臨川烈武王道規傳。 進號平北將軍。 高祖討劉毅，與宗之同會江陵，進號鎮北將軍，封南陽郡公，食邑二千五百戶。 子軌，一名象齒，爽之父也。 便弓馬，筋力絕人，為竟陵太守。 宗之自以非高祖舊隸，屢建大功，有自疑之心。 會司馬休之見討，猜懼，遂與休之北奔。 善於撫御，士民皆為盡力，衛送出境，盡室入羌，頃之病卒。 高祖定長安，軌為寧南將軍、荊州刺史、襄陽公，鎮長社。 世祖鎮襄陽，軌遣親人程整奉書，規欲歸順，自拔致誠，以昔殺劉康祖、徐湛之父，故不歸。 太祖累遣招納，許以為司州刺史。
Lu Shuang, whose childhood name was Nüsheng, came from Mei in Fufeng. His ancestor Zongzhi, styled Yanren, left home for Xiangyang in the last years of Jin Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era and eventually became prefect of Nan Commandery. In the first year of Yixi he took up arms, struck down the puppet inspector of Yong Province Huan Wei, and marched on Jiangling. For this service he was made General Who Assists the State and inspector of Yong Province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng with fifteen hundred households. When Huan Qian and Xun Lin threatened Jiangling, Zongzhi raced to its relief—the full account appears in the biography of Prince Daogui of Linchuan. He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North. When Emperor Gaozu marched against Liu Yi and joined Zongzhi at Jiangling, Zongzhi was made General Who Guards the North and Duke of Nanyang with twenty-five hundred households. His son Gui, also called Xiangchi, was Lu Shuang's father. He was expert with bow and horse and possessed strength beyond ordinary men. He became prefect of Jingling. Zongzhi knew he had not been one of Gaozu's old companions, yet he had won great victories again and again—and doubt began to eat at him. When Sima Xiuzhi was marked for punishment, fear overcame him and he fled north with Xiuzhi. He knew how to win men to him, and soldiers and civilians alike gave him their all. They escorted him beyond the frontier; his whole household went among the Qiang, and there he soon sickened and died. After Gaozu took Chang'an, Gui was made General Who Pacifies the South, inspector of Jing Province, and Duke of Xiangyang, with his seat at Changshe. When Emperor Xiaowu held Xiangyang, Gui sent his kinsman Cheng Zheng with a letter offering to surrender and swear loyalty of his own free will. But he had once killed Liu Kangzu and Xu Zhan's father, and for that he never came home. The founding emperor sent envoys again and again to win him over, promising him the post of Inspector of Si Province.
29
爽少有武藝，虜主拓跋燾知之，常置左右。 元嘉二十六年，軌死，爽為寧南將軍、荊州刺史、襄陽公，鎮長社。 幼染殊俗，無復華風。 粗中使酒，數有過失，燾將誅之。 爽有七弟秀，小字天念，頗有意略，才力過爽。 燾以充宿衛，甚知待之。 偽高梁王阿叔泥為芮芮所圍甚急，使秀往救，燾自率大眾繼其後。 燾未及至，秀已擊破之，拔阿叔泥而反。 燾壯其功，以為中書郎，封廣陵侯。 或告燾，鄴民欲據城反，復遣檢察，并燒石虎殘宮殿。 秀常乘驛往反，是時病還遲，為燾所詰讓，秀復恐懼。 燾尋南寇，因從渡河。
Lu Shuang had shown martial talent from boyhood, and Tuoba Tao, the Wei ruler, kept him close at hand. In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, after Gui died, Shuang was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Jing Province, and Duke of Xiangyang, with his headquarters at Changshe. Raised among alien customs from childhood, he had lost every trace of civilized Chinese bearing. Coarse in manner and prone to drunken outbursts, he offended again and again until Tao was ready to put him to death. Shuang's seventh brother, Xiu—courtesy name Tiannian—was a man of real strategic sense, and his talent and force outmatched Shuang's own. Tao placed him in the palace guard and showed him exceptional favor. When the puppet Prince of Gaoliang, Ashuni, was hard pressed by a Rouran siege, Tao sent Xiu to the rescue and followed with a great army of his own. Xiu had already broken the enemy, pulled Ashuni free, and returned before Tao even arrived. Impressed by the feat, Tao made him a Secretariat Gentleman and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Guangling. When word reached Tao that the people of Ye meant to seize the city and revolt, he sent Xiu out once more to investigate—and Xiu burned the ruined palaces of Shi Hu as well. Xiu was constantly riding the post roads back and forth; this time illness delayed his return, and Tao rebuked him. Fear seized Xiu again. Not long after, when Tao marched south on campaign, Xiu crossed the river with him.
30
先是，程天祚為虜所沒，燾引置左右，與秀囗寬，勸令歸降，秀納之。 天祚，廣平人，為殿中將軍，有武力。 元嘉二十七年，助戍彭城，會世祖遣府劉泰之輕軍襲虜於汝陽，天祚督戰，戰敗被創，為虜所獲。 天祚妙善針術，燾深加愛賞，或與同輿，常不離於側，封為南安公。 燾北還蕃，天祚因其沈醉，偽若受使督切後軍者，所至輕罰。 天祚為燾所愛，群虜並畏之，莫敢問，因得逃歸，後為山陽太守。 太宗初，與四方同反，事在薛安都傳。
Earlier, Cheng Tianzuo had fallen into enemy hands. Tao kept him at court, and he and Xiu grew close; Tianzuo urged Xiu to defect south, and Xiu agreed. Tianzuo came from Guangping, held the post of Palace Guard General, and was a man of proven fighting strength. In Yuanjia twenty-seven he helped hold Pengcheng. When Emperor Xiaowu sent Liu Taizhi's light column from his staff to hit the enemy at Ruyang, Tianzuo commanded the fight, was beaten and wounded, and taken captive. Tianzuo was a master of needle-cure; Tao doted on him, sometimes sharing his carriage and never letting him stray far, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Nan'an. On the northern march home, Tianzuo waited until Tao was drunk, then posed as an envoy overseeing the rearguard and let offenders off lightly wherever he passed. Because Tao favored him, the northerners feared him too, and no one dared challenge him—so he slipped away and made it back south. He later became Administrator of Shanyang. At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he joined the general revolt; the full account appears in the biography of Xue Andu.
31
燾始南行，遣爽隨永昌王庫仁真向壽陽，與弟瑜共破劉祖於尉武，仍至瓜步，始得與秀定歸南之謀。 燾還至湖陸，爽等請曰：「奴與南有仇，每兵來，常慮禍及墳墓，乞共迎喪，還葬國都。 」虜群下於其主稱奴，猶中國稱臣也。 燾許之。 長社戍虜有六七百人，爽譎之曰：「南更有軍，可遣三百騎往界上參聽。 」騎去，爽率腹心夜擊餘虜，盡殺之，馳入虎牢。
When Tao first marched south, he sent Shuang with Prince Yongchang Kuren Zhen toward Shouyang. Shuang and his brother Yu routed Liu Zu at Yuwu, pushed on to Guabu, and there at last fixed with Xiu their plan to go home. As Tao withdrew to Hulin, Shuang and the others pleaded: "Your slave is at odds with the south; whenever armies come, we dread for our ancestors' graves. We beg permission to go together and bring our dead home for burial in the capital." Among the northerners, retainers call themselves "slave" before their lord—the same as "subject" in the Middle Kingdom. Tao agreed. Six or seven hundred northerners held the Changshe garrison. Shuang tricked them: "There are more southern troops ahead—send three hundred riders to the border to scout." Once the riders were gone, Shuang led his inner circle in a night strike, slaughtered every man left behind, and raced into Hulao.
32
爽唯第三弟在北，餘家屬悉自隨，率部曲及願從合千餘家奔汝南。 遣秀從許昌還壽陽，奉辭於南平王鑠曰：「爽、秀得罪晉朝，負釁三世，生長絕域，遠身胡虜，兄弟闔門，淪點偽授，殞命不可，還國無因。 近係南雲，傾屬東日，蓋猶痿人思步，盲者願明。 嵩、霍咫尺，江、河匪遠，夷庚壅塞，隔同天地，痛心疾首，書慨宵悲。 虜主倡狂，豺豕其志，虐遍華、戎，怨結幽顯。 自盱眙旋軍，亡殪過半，昏酣沈湎，恣性肆身。 爽、秀等因民之憤，藉將旅之願，齊契義奮，梟馘醜徒，馮恃皇威，肅清逋穢，牢、洛諸城，指期克定。 規以涓塵，微雪夙負，方當束骸北闕，待戮司寇，懦節未申，伏心邊表。 明大王殿下以叡茂居蕃，文武兼姿，遠邇欽傾，承風聞德，願垂援拯，以慰虔望。 老弱百口，先遣歸庇。 逼逼丹心，仰希懷遠。 謹遣同義潁川聶元初奉詞陳聞。 」鑠馳驛以聞，上大說，下詔曰：「偽寧南將軍魯爽、中書郎魯秀，志幹列到，忠誠久著，撫茲福先，闔門效款，招集義銳，梟剪獯醜，肅定邊城，獻馘象魏。 雖宣孟之去翟歸晉，頹當之出胡入漢，方之此日，曾何足云。 朕實嘉之，宜即授任，逞其忠略。 爽可督司州、陳留、東郡、濟陰、濮陽五郡諸軍事、征虜將軍、司州刺史。 秀可輔國將軍、滎陽、潁川二郡太守。 其諸子弟及同契士庶，委征虜府以時申言，詳加酬敘。 」爽至汝南，加督豫州之義陽、宋安二郡軍事，領義陽內史，將軍、刺史如故。 秀參右將軍南平王鑠軍事、汝陰內史，將軍如故。 餘弟姪竝授官爵，賞賜資給甚厚。 爽北鎮義陽。 北來部曲凡六千八百八十三人，是歲二十八年也。 虜毀其墳墓。
Only Shuang's third brother stayed behind in the north; the rest of the clan came with him. With their retainers and every household that would follow—more than a thousand in all—they fled to Runan. He sent Xiu from Xuchang back to Shouyang with a letter to Prince Liu Shuo of Nanping: "Shuang and Xiu have sinned against the Jin court and borne shame for three generations. We grew up in a far land and cast our lot with the Hu; our whole brotherhood fell under false northern titles. We could not choose death, yet had no path home." "Lately we have been tied to southern clouds and turn every hope toward the eastern sun—as a cripple longs to walk, as the blind longs for sight." "Song and Huo stand within reach; the Yangtze and the Yellow River are not far—yet the roads are choked shut, and we are parted as if by heaven and earth itself. Our hearts break and our heads pound; we write through the night in grief." "The northern lord raves like a mad beast, his heart that of wolf and hog; his cruelty falls on Chinese and barbarian alike, and wrath binds the living to the dead." "Since he withdrew from Xuyi, more than half his army lies unburied; he sinks in drunken stupor and indulges every appetite." "Shuang, Xiu, and our men rode the people's anger and the army's will, struck together in righteous fury, and took the heads of the enemy. Trusting in the emperor's might, we have cleared the rebel stain—Hulao and Luoyang will fall on schedule." "We offer this mote of service to repay, however slightly, our old debt; we should bind ourselves and present our bodies at the northern gate for the Minister of Justice to punish. Our feeble loyalty has not yet been shown—we lay our hearts bare at the border." "Your Highness holds your fief with wise brilliance, skilled in both pen and sword; men near and far look to you. Hearing your name on the wind, we beg you to reach out and save us, and ease our desperate hope." "We have sent ahead our hundred dependents, old and weak, to seek your protection." "Our loyal hearts press close; we look up, hoping you will shelter the far-flung and forsaken." "We respectfully dispatch Nie Yuanchu of Yingchuan, who shares our cause, to lay these words before you." Liu Shuo sent word by urgent relay. The emperor was delighted and issued an edict: "The former northern General Who Pacifies the South, Lu Shuang, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Xiu—their will and talent stand out, their loyalty long known. First among the blessed, their whole house has submitted; rallying loyal troops, they have cut down the savage foe, secured the border cities, and sent trophies to the imperial gate." Even Xuanni's flight from Di to Jin, or Tuodang's passage from the Hu into Han—what are such old tales beside this day's deed? I am truly pleased with them. Let them be appointed immediately and given full scope for their loyal designs. Shuang shall oversee military affairs in Si, Chenliu, Dongjun, Jiyin, and Puyang—five commanderies—as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Si Province. Xiu shall be General Who Supports the State and Administrator of Xingyang and Yingchuan. Their brothers, nephews, and every ally who joined the cause shall be reported in due course to the Conquest General's office for proper reward. When Shuang reached Runan, he was also given command over Yiyang and Song'an in Yuzhou and made Interior Administrator of Yiyang; his general's rank and inspectorship stood as before. Xiu was attached to Prince Liu Shuo of Nanping as staff officer to the General of the Right and made Interior Administrator of Ruyin; his general's rank was unchanged. The other brothers and nephews all received offices and titles, along with generous gifts and stipends. Shuang took up northern garrison duty at Yiyang. The followers who came from the north totaled 6,883 households; it was Yuanjia twenty-eight. The northerners desecrated and destroyed their family tombs.
33
明年四月入朝，時燾已死，上更謀經略。 五月，遣爽、秀、程天祚等率步騎並荊州軍甲士四萬，出許、洛。 八月，虜長社戍主永平公禿髮幡乃同棄城走。 進向大索戍，戍主偽豫州刺史跋僕蘭曰：「爽勇而無防，我今出城，必輕來據之，設伏檀山，必可禽也。 」爽果夜進，秀諫不止，馳往繼之。 比曉，虜騎夾發，賴秀縱兵力戰，虜乃退還虎牢。 爽因進攻之，本期舟師入河，斷其水門。 王玄謨攻碻磝不拔，敗退，水軍不至，爽亦收眾南還。 轉鬬數百里，至曲彊，虜候其饑疲，盡銳來攻，爽身自奮擊，虜乃退走。
The next year, in the fourth month, he came to court. Tao was already dead, and the emperor turned again to plans of conquest. In the fifth month he sent Shuang, Xiu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others at the head of infantry and cavalry, joined by forty thousand armored men from Jing Province, marching out from Xu and Luo. In the eighth month the northern garrison commander at Changshe, Duke of Yongping Tufa Fan, abandoned the city and fled. As they pushed toward the Dasuo garrison, its commander—the northern Inspector of Yu, Ba Fulan—said: "Shuang is brave but careless. If I leave the city now, he will surely come in lightly and take it. Ambush him on Tanshan and we can take him for certain." Shuang did march by night. Xiu warned against it but could not hold him back and rode hard to follow. At daybreak northern cavalry struck from both sides. Only Xiu's all-out fight drove them back to Hulao. Shuang pressed on with the siege. The plan had been for the river fleet to enter the stream and seal the water gates. Wang Xuanmo failed to take Que'ao and fell back in defeat; the fleet never came, and Shuang gathered his men and retreated south. They fought a running battle for hundreds of li until they reached Quqiang. The northerners, waiting until hunger and fatigue had worn them down, threw in their best troops; Shuang fought at the front himself and at last drove them off.
34
爽直出歷陽，自采石濟軍，與質水陸俱下。 爽遣弟瑜守蒙蘢，歷陽太守張幼緒請擊瑜，世祖配以兵力。 遣左軍將薛安都步騎為前驅，別遣水軍入淵，分路竝會。 安都進次大峴，爽已立營。 世祖以賊強壘固，未可輕拔，使量宜進止。 幼緒便引軍退還，下獄。 更遣驍騎將軍垣護之代幼緒據歷陽。 鎮軍將軍沈慶之係安都進軍，與爽相遇於小峴。 爽親自前，將戰，而飲酒過醉，安都刺爽倒馬，左右范雙斬首，傳送京都。 瑜亦為部下所斬送，進平壽陽，子弟竝伏誅。
Shuang marched straight for Liyang, ferried his army across at Caishi, and moved downriver by land and water together with Zang Zhi. Shuang left his brother Yu to hold Menglong. Zhang Youxu, Administrator of Liyang, asked to strike Yu, and Emperor Xiaowu gave him additional forces. He sent Xue Andu of the Left Army ahead with infantry and cavalry, and a separate flotilla into Lake Chao—the columns were to meet from different directions. Andu moved up and halted at Great Xian Pass; Shuang had already pitched camp. Emperor Xiaowu judged the enemy strong and the fort too solid for a reckless assault, and told him to advance or hold as he saw fit. Youxu simply pulled his men back—and was thrown into prison. He then sent the Swift Cavalry General Yuan Huzhi to replace Youxu and hold Liyang. The Pacification Army General Shen Qingzhi, moving up behind Andu, encountered Shuang at Little Xian Pass. Shuang rode forward himself to give battle—but he was dead drunk. Andu speared him from his saddle; his attendant Fan Shuang took his head and sent it to the capital. Yu was cut down by his own men and his head sent in. The army pushed on, took Shouyang, and put every brother and son to death.
35
義宣初舉兵，召秀加節，進號征虜將軍，當繼諶之俱下。 雝州刺史朱脩之起兵奉順，更遣秀擊脩之。 王玄謨聞之，喜曰：「魯秀不來，臧質易與耳。 」秀至襄陽，大敗而反。 會益州刺史劉秀之遣軍襲江陵，秀擊破之。 義宣還江陵，秀與共北走，眾叛且盡。 秀向城，上射之，中箭，赴水死，軍人宗敬叔、康僧念斬首，傳京邑。
When Liu Yixuan first rebelled, he called Xiu to him, gave him the staff of command, promoted him to General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and set him to follow Liu Zunzhi south. Zhu Xiuzhi, Inspector of Yong Province, took up arms for the throne; Yixuan sent Xiu out again to crush him. When Wang Xuanmo heard, he said with relief: "If Lu Xiu stays away, Zang Zhi will be easy meat." Xiu reached Xiangyang—and was routed on the return march. About then Liu Xiuzhi of Yi Province sent a column to strike Jiangling; Xiu beat them back. Yixuan fell back to Jiangling. Xiu fled north with him while men deserted until almost none were left. Xiu turned toward the wall; arrows from above found him. He plunged into the water and drowned. Zong Jingshu and Kang Sengnian, common soldiers, took his head and sent it to the capital.
36
贈韋處穆、楊元駒給事中，庾騰之員外散騎侍郎。 爽初南歸，秀以爽武人，不閑吏職，白太祖請處穆為長史以輔爽，太祖以補司馬，後轉長史云。
Posthumous appointments followed: Wei Chumu and Yang Yuanju as Attendants Within the Yellow Gates, Yu Tengzhi as Supernumerary Palace Cadet. When Shuang first came south, Xiu—knowing his brother was a fighting man with no taste for paperwork—asked the founding emperor to assign Wei Chumu as Chief Clerk to guide him. The emperor first made Chumu Military Adviser and later promoted him to Chief Clerk.
37
沈攸之，字仲達，吳興武康人，司空慶之從父兄子也。 父叔仁，為衡陽王義季征西長史，兼行參軍，領隊，又隨義季鎮彭城，度征北府。 攸之少孤貧，元嘉二十七年，索虜南寇，發三吳民丁，攸之亦被發。 既至京都，詣領軍將軍劉遵考，求補白丁隊主。 遵考謂之曰：「君形陋，不堪隊主。 」因隨慶之征討。 二十九年，征西陽蠻，始補隊主。 巴口建義，南中郎府板長史，兼行參軍。 新亭之戰，身被重創，事寧，為太尉行參軍，封平洛縣五等侯。 隨府轉大司馬行參軍。 晉世京邑二岸，揚州舊置都部從事，分掌二縣非違，永初以後罷省，孝建三年，復置其職。 攸之掌北岸，會稽孔璨掌南岸，後又罷。 攸之遷員外散騎侍郎。 又隨慶之征廣陵，屢有功，被箭破骨。 世祖以其善戰，配以仇池步矟。 事平，當加厚賞，為慶之所抑，遷太子旅賁中郎，攸之甚恨之。 七年，遭母憂，葬畢，起為龍驤將軍、武康令。
Shen Youzhi, styled Zhongda, came from Wukang in Wuxing. He was a cousin on his father's side of Shen Qingzhi, Minister of Works. His father Shuren had been Chief Clerk on the western campaign staff of Prince Liu Yiji of Hengyang, also serving as acting adjutant and company leader; he later followed Yiji to Pengcheng and moved on to the Northern Expedition headquarters. Youzhi lost his parents early and grew up poor. In Yuanjia twenty-seven, when the northern armies came south, the Three Wu districts were levied for militia—and Youzhi was drafted. Reaching the capital, he went to Liu Zunkao, General of the Central Army, and asked to be made squad leader of a raw conscript unit. Zunkao told him, "You are too plain-looking to lead a squad." So he went out instead with Qingzhi on campaign. In the twenty-ninth year, on the Xiyang campaign, he was at last made squad leader. When the revolt broke out at Bakou, the Southern Colonel's staff made him Chief Clerk and acting adjutant. At Xinting he took heavy wounds. After peace returned, he became acting adjutant to the Grand Marshal and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Pingluo. He followed the command staff and was transferred to acting adjutant under the Grand Marshal. Under Jin the capital's two riverbanks had each been supervised—the old Yangzhou post of Capital District Attendant split oversight of the two counties' misconduct. After Yongchu the office lapsed; in Xiaojian three it was revived. Youzhi handled the north bank; Kong Can of Kuaiji the south. The post was abolished again afterward. Youzhi was moved to Supernumerary Palace Cadet. He went out again with Qingzhi against Guangling, earned merit again and again, and took an arrow that splintered bone. Emperor Xiaowu, impressed by his fighting, assigned him a Qichi foot-lance. When the war ended he should have been richly rewarded, but Qingzhi blocked it; he was posted instead as Central Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and Youzhi nursed a deep grudge. In the seventh year he mourned his mother; once the rites were done he was recalled as Dragon Cavalry General and Magistrate of Wukang.
38
前廢帝景和元年，除豫章王子尚車騎中兵參軍，直閣，與宗越、譚金等並為廢帝所寵，誅戮群公，攸之等皆為之用命。 封東興縣侯，食邑五百戶。 尋遷右軍將軍，增邑百戶。 太宗即位，以例削封。 宗越、譚金等謀反，攸之復召入直閣，除東海太守。 未拜，會四方反叛，南賊已次近道，以攸之為寧朔將軍、尋陽太守，率軍據虎檻。 時王玄謨為大統，未發。 前鋒有五軍在虎檻，五軍後又絡驛繼至，每夜各立姓號，不相稟受。 攸之謂軍吏曰：「今眾軍姓號不同，若有耕夫漁父，夜相呵叱，便致駭亂，取敗之道也。 」乃就一軍請號，眾咸從之。 殷孝祖為前鋒都督，而大失人情，攸之內撫將士，外諧群帥，眾並倚賴之。 時南賊前鋒鍾沖之、薛常寶等屯據赭圻，殷孝祖率眾軍攻之，為流矢所中死，軍主范潛率五百人投賊，人情震駭，並謂攸之宜代孝祖為統。 時建安王休仁屯虎檻，揔統眾軍，聞孝祖死，遣寧朔將軍江方興、龍驤將軍劉靈遺各率三千人赴赭圻。 攸之以為孝祖既死，賊有乘勝之心，明日若不更攻，則示之以弱。 方興名位相亞，必不為己下，軍政不一，致敗之由。 乃率諸軍主詣方興，謂之曰：「四方並反，國家所保，無復百里之地。 唯有殷孝祖為朝廷所委賴，鋒鏑裁交，輿尸而反，文武喪氣，朝野危心。 事之濟否，唯在明旦一戰，戰若不捷，則大事去矣。 詰朝之事，諸人咸謂吾應統之，自卜懦薄，幹略不辦及卿，今輒相推為統。 但當相與戮力爾。 」方興甚悅。 攸之既出，諸軍主並尤之，攸之曰：「卿忘廉、藺、寇、賈之事邪？ 吾本以濟國活家，豈計彼此之升降。 且我能下彼，彼必不能下我，共濟艱難，豈可自厝同異！ 」明旦進戰，自寅訖午，大破賊於赭圻城外，追奔至姥山，分遣水軍乘勢進討； 又破其水軍，拔胡、白二城。
In the first year of Jinghe under the Deposed Emperor, he became Central Army Adjutant on Prince Liu Zishang of Yuzhang's staff and served in the palace guard. He, Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and the rest were the Deposed Emperor's favorites; when the great lords were butchered, Youzhi and his fellows did the killing. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing with five hundred households. Soon he rose to General of the Right Army, with a hundred more households added to his fief. When Emperor Ming took the throne, his fief was trimmed by the usual rule. When Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and the others plotted treason, Youzhi was called back to the palace guard and made Administrator of Donghai. Before he could assume the post, revolts erupted everywhere and southern enemy forces were already closing in. Youzhi was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Xunyang and led an army to seize Hujian. Wang Xuannmo was then supreme commander, but his army had not yet marched. Five vanguard armies were already at Hujian, and five more kept arriving in relays. Each night they used different family names and watchwords and took orders from no one else. Youzhi told the staff officers: "Every unit has its own watchwords now. If a farmer or fisherman shouted in the night, we'd panic each other—that's how armies lose." He asked one army for its watchword, and the rest all adopted it. Yin Xiaozu commanded the vanguard but had badly alienated the ranks. Youzhi won over the soldiers and kept the other generals on side, and all looked to him. The rebel vanguard under Zhong Chongzhi and Xue Changbao held Zheqi. Yin Xiaozu led the combined force against them, took a stray arrow, and died. Commander Fan Qian defected with five hundred men. The shock was general, and everyone agreed Youzhi should take Xiaozu's command. Prince Liu Xiuren of Jian'an held Hujian as overall commander. When he heard Xiaozu was dead, he sent Jiang Fangxing, General Who Pacifies the North, and Liu Lingyi, Dragon Cavalry General, each with three thousand men, to Zheqi. Youzhi reasoned that with Xiaozu dead the enemy would press their advantage, and if the army did not attack again the next day it would look weak. Fangxing was his equal in rank and would never take orders from him. Split command was a recipe for defeat. He took the army commanders to Fangxing and said: "The realm is in revolt on every side. The court holds barely a hundred li of ground. Yin Xiaozu alone was the man the court counted on. Blades had barely met when they brought his body back. Officials and soldiers lost heart; the whole realm trembled. Success or ruin hangs on tomorrow's fight. If we lose, everything is over. For tomorrow's battle everyone says I should lead, but I know I'm too timid and dull—I can't match your ability. I'm handing you the command. We must only fight as one. Fangxing was delighted. When Youzhi left, the commanders all blamed him. He said: "Have you forgotten Lian Po and Lin Xiangru, Kou Xun and Jia Fu? I'm trying to save the realm and my family, not to jockey for rank. I can yield to him; he could never yield to me. In a crisis like this we can't afford to split over pride! The next morning they attacked. From dawn until midday they smashed the enemy outside Zheqi, chased them to Laoshan, and sent the fleet forward to exploit the rout; they broke the rebel fleet as well and took the cities of Hu and Bai.
39
尋假攸之節，進號輔國將軍，代孝祖督前鋒諸軍事。 薛常寶在赭圻食盡，南賊大帥劉胡屯濃湖，以囊盛米繫流查及船腹，陽覆船，順風流下，以餉赭圻。 攸之疑其有異，遣人取船及流查，大得囊米。 攸之從子懷寶，為賊將帥，在赭圻，遣親人楊公贊齎密書招誘攸之，攸之斬公贊，封懷寶書呈太宗。 尋克赭圻，遷使持節、督雍、梁、南、北秦四州、郢州之竟陵諸軍事、冠軍將軍、領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
Soon Youzhi received command authority, was promoted to General Who Supports the State, and replaced Xiaozu as commander of the vanguard. Xue Changbao at Zheqi was out of provisions. The rebel commander Liu Hu at Nonghu loaded rice into sacks, lashed them to driftwood and boat hulls, disguised them as wreckage, and sent them downwind to feed Zheqi. Youzhi smelled a trick, had the boats and driftwood seized, and captured a large haul of rice. Youzhi's nephew Huaibao served the rebels at Zheqi and sent a relative, Yang Gongzan, with a secret letter to win him over. Youzhi had Gongzan executed, sealed Huaibao's letter, and sent it to Emperor Ming. Zheqi fell soon after. He was made Bearer of the Insignia of Authority with command over Yong, Liang, Southern and Northern Qin, and Jingling in Ying Province, Champion General, Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yong.
40
袁顗復率大眾來入鵲尾，相持既久，軍主張興世越鵲尾上據錢溪，劉胡自攻之。 攸之率諸將攻濃湖，顗遣人傳唱錢溪已平，眾竝懼。 攸之曰：「不然。 若錢溪實敗，萬人中應有逃亡得還者。 必是彼戰失利，唱空聲以惑眾耳。 」勒軍中不得妄動。 錢溪信尋至，果大破賊。 攸之悉以錢溪所送胡軍耳鼻示之，顗駭懼，急追胡還。 攸之諸軍悉力進攻，多所斬獲，日暮引歸。 鵲尾食盡，遣千人往南陵迎米，為臺軍所破，燒其資實，胡於是棄眾而奔，顗亦叛走。 赭圻、濃湖之平也，賊軍委棄資財，珍貨殷積，諸軍各競收斂，以強弱為少多。 唯攸之、張興世約勒所部，不犯秋毫，諸將以此多之。 攸之進平尋陽，徙監郢州諸軍事、前將軍、郢州刺史，持節如故。 不拜，遷中領軍，封貞陽縣公，食邑二千戶。
Yuan Yi returned with a large army into Quewei. The standoff dragged on until Zhang Xingshi slipped upstream past Quewei and took Qianxi. Liu Hu attacked him in person. Youzhi led the generals against Nonghu. Yi spread rumors that Qianxi had fallen, and panic spread through the ranks. Youzhi said: "Not so. If Qianxi had really been lost, some of ten thousand men would have fled back by now. They lost the fight and are spreading false news to unsettle us. He forbade the army to move. Word from Qianxi came soon after: the enemy had been crushed. Youzhi paraded the ears and noses of Liu Hu's men sent from Qianxi. Yi was terrified and called Liu Hu back at once. Youzhi's forces attacked with everything they had, killing and capturing many. At dusk they pulled back. Quewei's stores were exhausted. A thousand men sent to Nanling for grain were beaten by the imperial force and their supplies burned. Liu Hu abandoned his army and fled; Yi broke and ran as well. After Zheqi and Nonghu fell, the rebels left fortunes behind. Every unit scrambled for loot, each taking what its strength allowed. Only Youzhi and Zhang Xingshi kept their men in line and took not the slightest thing. The other generals respected them for it. Youzhi went on to take Xunyang. He was made overseer of Ying Province's armies, Forward General, and Inspector of Ying, keeping his command authority. He declined the post. He was made Central Palace Guard Commander, created Duke of Zhenyang with a fief of two thousand households.
41
時四方皆已平定，徐州刺史薛安都據彭城請降，上雖相酬許，而辭旨簡略。 攸之前將軍，置佐吏，假節，與鎮軍將軍張永以重兵徵安都。 安都懼，要引索虜； 索虜引大眾援之。 攸之等米船在呂梁，又遣軍主王穆之上民口； 穆之為虜攻覆米船，又破運車於武原，攸之等引退，為虜所乘，又值寒雪，士眾墮指十二三。 留長水校尉王玄載守下邳，積射將軍沈韶守宿豫，睢陵、淮陽亦置戍，攸之還淮陰。 免官，以公領職。 復求進討，上不聽，入朝面陳，又不許，復歸淮陰。 三年六月，自率運送米下邳，并鑿四周深塹，遣龍驤將軍垣護之領民口還淮陰。
By then the realm was quiet. Xue Andu, Inspector of Xuzhou, held Pengcheng and offered to surrender. The emperor answered yes, but coldly and in few words. Youzhi became Forward General with a full staff and temporary command authority. He and Zhang Yong, General Who Guards the Army, marched against Andu with a large army. Andu panicked and called in the Northern Wei; the Wei sent a large relief force. Youzhi's grain fleet was at Lüliang, and he sent Wang Muzhi upstream with the civilian evacuees; The Wei attacked Muzhi, sank the grain boats, and smashed the supply train at Wuyuan. Youzhi pulled back under pursuit, and in the blizzard one man in ten lost fingers to frostbite. Wang Xuanzai, Commandant of the Long River, was left at Xiapi; Shen Shao, General of Accumulated Archers, at Suyu; garrisons were posted at Suiling and Huaiyang. Youzhi withdrew to Huaiyin. He was stripped of office but kept his post in his ducal capacity. He asked again to take the offensive; the emperor refused. He came to court to plead in person and was turned down again. He went back to Huaiyin. In the sixth month of the third year he personally convoyed grain to Xiapi and dug deep trenches all around. He sent Yuan Huzhi, Dragon Cavalry General, to escort the civilians back to Huaiyin.
42
時軍主陳顯達當領千兵守下邳，攸之留待顯達至，虜遣清泗間人詐告攸之云：「安都欲降，求軍迎接。 」攸之副吳喜納其說，咸謂宜遣千人參之，既而來者轉多，喜所執彌固。 攸之乃集來者告之，語曰：「薛徐州早宜還朝，今能爾，深副本望。 但遣子弟一人來，便當遣大軍相接。 君諸人既有志心，若能與薛子弟俱來者，皆即假君以本鄉縣，唯意所欲； 如其不爾，無為空勞往還。 」自此一去不反。
Chen Xianda was due to take a thousand men to hold Xiapi, and Youzhi waited for him. The Wei sent agents from the Qing-Si region with a false report: "Andu wants to surrender and asks for an escort. Youzhi's deputy Wu Xi believed it; everyone said a thousand men should go. More messengers kept coming, and Xi dug in harder. Youzhi summoned the messengers and said: "Inspector Xue of Xuzhou should have come back to court long ago. If he's ready now, that's exactly what I hoped for. Send one of his sons or brothers, and I'll send a large force to meet him. If you're sincere and come with Xue's kin, I'll appoint each of you magistrate of whatever home district you choose; otherwise don't waste the trip. None of them ever came back.
43
其年秋，太宗復令攸之進圍彭城。 攸之以清泗既乾，糧運不繼，固執以為非宜，往反者七。 上大怒，詔攸之曰：「卿春中求伐彭城，吾恐軍士疲勞，且去冬奔散，人心未宜復用，不許卿所啟。 今便不肯為吾行邪？ 卿若不行，便可使吳喜獨去。 」攸之懼，乃奉旨進軍。 行至遲墟，上悔，追軍令反。 攸之還至下邳，而陳顯達於睢口為虜所破，龍驤將軍姜產之、司徒參軍高遵世戰沒。 虜追攸之甚急，因交戰，被矟創，會暮，引軍入顯達壘，夕眾散，八月十八日也。 攸之棄眾南奔。
That autumn Emperor Ming ordered Youzhi to besiege Pengcheng again. Youzhi argued that the Qing and Si rivers were dry and supplies could not be kept up, and insisted the move was wrong. They exchanged messages seven times. The emperor was furious and wrote to Youzhi: "In spring you asked to attack Pengcheng. I refused because the men were exhausted and last winter's rout had broken their morale. Now you won't march when I order it? If you won't go, I'll send Wu Xi by himself. Youzhi was alarmed and marched as ordered. At Chixu the emperor changed his mind and recalled the army. Youzhi got back to Xiapi, but Chen Xianda had been beaten at Suikou. Jiang Chanazhi, Dragon Cavalry General, and Gao Zunshi, staff officer to the Minister of Education, were killed. The Wei pressed hard on Youzhi. In the fighting he took a spear wound. At dusk he withdrew into Xianda's camp; by nightfall his force had broken. It was the eighteenth of the eighth month. Youzhi abandoned his army and fled south.
44
初，吳興丘幼弼、丘隆先、沈誕、沈榮守、吳陸道量，並以文記之才隨攸之，及張永北討，永一奔，攸之再敗，幼弼等並皆陷沒。 攸之之還淮陰，以為持節、假冠軍將軍、行南兗州刺史。 追贈姜產之左軍將軍，高遵世屯騎校尉。
Earlier, the Wuxing literati Qiu Youbi, Qiu Longxian, Shen Dan, Shen Rongshou, and Wu Ludao had served with Youzhi. Zhang Yong fled once in the northern campaign and Youzhi lost twice; Youbi and the rest all died. On returning to Huaiyin, Youzhi was made Bearer of the Insignia of Authority, Acting Champion General, and provisional Inspector of Southern Yan. Jiang Chanazhi was posthumously made Left Army General; Gao Zunshi, Commandant of Garrison Cavalry.
45
四年，徵攸之為吳興太守，辭不拜。 乃除左衛將軍，領太子中庶子。 五年，出為持節、監郢州諸軍、郢州刺史。 為政刻暴，或鞭士大夫，上佐以下有忤意，輒面加詈辱。 將吏一人亡叛，同籍符伍充代者十餘人。 而曉達吏事，自強不息，士民畏憚，人莫敢欺。 聞有虎，輒自圍捕，往無不得，一日或得兩三。 若逼暮不獲禽，則宿昔圍守，須曉自出。 賦斂嚴苦，徵發無度，繕治船舸，營造器甲。 自至夏口，便有異圖。 六年，進監豫州之西陽、司州之義陽二郡軍事，進號鎮軍將軍。
In the fourth year he was called to be Administrator of Wuxing and refused the appointment. He was made Left Guard General and Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent instead. In the fifth year he was posted as Bearer of the Insignia of Authority, commander of Ying Province's armies, and Inspector of Ying. He ruled with brutal severity, sometimes flogging gentry officials. Anyone from senior aides down who crossed him was insulted to his face. If a single officer or clerk deserted, more than ten men from his household register and neighborhood group were drafted to replace him. Yet he knew administration inside out and drove himself without rest. Officials and commoners feared him, and no one dared cheat him. When word came of a tiger he hunted it himself. He never missed; some days he took two or three. If he had no kill by dusk, he kept the ring through the night and was out again at first light. He taxed and conscripted without mercy, repaired ships, and forged arms and armor. From the moment he reached Xiakou he was plotting something else. In the sixth year he was given command over Xiyang in Yu and Yiyang in Si and promoted to General Who Guards the Army.
46
江州刺史桂陽王休範密有異志，以微旨動攸之，使道士陳公昭作天公書一函，題云「沈丞相」，送付攸之門者； 攸之不開書，推得公昭，送之朝廷。 後廢帝元徽二年，休範舉兵襲京邑，攸之謂僚佐曰：「桂陽今反朝廷，必聲云與攸之同。 若不顛沛勤王，必增朝野之惑。 」於是遣軍主孫同、沈懷奧興軍馳下，受郢州刺史晉熙王燮節度。 同等始過夏口，會休範平，還。 進攸之號征西大將軍、開府儀同三司，固讓開府。
Prince Liu Xiufan of Guiyang, Inspector of Jiang, was secretly plotting rebellion. He tried to win Youzhi over by having the Daoist Chen Gongzhao write a "Letter from the Lord of Heaven" addressed to "Chancellor Shen" and left at Youzhi's gate; Youzhi never opened the letter, tracked down Gongzhao, and handed him over to the court. In the second year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, Xiufan rebelled and struck the capital. Youzhi told his staff: "Guiyang will claim we're in this together. If we don't march to the emperor's aid at once, court and country will only grow more confused. He sent Sun Tong and Shen Huai'ao downstream at speed under Liu Xie, Prince of Jinxi and Inspector of Ying. They had barely passed Xiakou when Xiufan was defeated, and turned back. Youzhi was promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the West with Bespoke Staff Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; he declined the bespoke staff.
47
攸之自擅閫外，朝廷疑憚之，累欲徵入，慮不受命，乃止。 群公稱皇太后令，遣中使問攸之曰：「久勞於外，宜還京輦，然任寄之重，換代殊為未易，還止之宜，一以相委。 」欲以觀察其意。 攸之答曰：「荷國重恩，名器至此，自惟凡陋，本無廊廟之姿。 至如戍防一蕃，撲討蠻蜓，可強充斯任。 雖自上如此，豈敢厝心去留，歸還之事，伏聽朝旨。 」朝廷逾懾憚，徵議遂息。 四年，建平王景素據京城反，攸之復應朝廷； 景素尋平。
Youzhi held unchecked power on the frontier. The court distrusted and feared him, wanted repeatedly to recall him, but feared he would refuse—and let the matter drop. The senior ministers, citing the Empress Dowager's order, sent an envoy to ask Youzhi: "You've been abroad too long and should return to the capital—but your post is hard to replace. Whether you come back or stay is entirely up to you. They meant to test his intentions. Youzhi answered: "The state has honored me beyond measure. I know I'm a plain man, never cut out for high office. Guarding a frontier and fighting barbarians—that much I can manage. Even though Your Majesty puts it that way, I wouldn't presume to decide for myself. I'll do whatever the court orders. The court grew only more wary, and the recall was dropped. In the fourth year Prince Liu Jingsu of Jianping rebelled and held the capital; Youzhi again rallied to the court; Jingsu was crushed soon after.
48
初元嘉中，巴東、建平二郡，軍府富實，與江夏、竟陵、武陵並為名郡。 世祖于江夏置郢州，郡罷軍府，竟陵、武陵亦並殘壞，巴東、建平為峽中蠻所破，至是民人流散，存者無幾。 其年春，攸之遣軍入峽討蠻帥田五郡等。 及景素反，攸之急追峽中軍，巴東太守劉攘兵、建平太守劉道欣並疑攸之自有異志，阻兵斷峽，不聽軍下。 時攘兵元子天賜為荊州西曹，攸之遣天賜譬說之，令其解甲，一無所問。 攘兵見天賜，知景素實反，乃釋甲謝愆，攸之待之如故，後以攘兵為府司馬。 劉道欣堅守建平，攘兵譬說不回，乃與伐蠻軍攻之，破建平，斬道欣。
In the Yuanjia era, Badong and Jianping—with their military headquarters—were wealthy districts, ranked with Jiangxia, Jingling, and Wuling among the great commanderies. Emperor Xiaowu made Ying Province at Jiangxia, abolished the commanderies and closed the military headquarters. Jingling and Wuling fell to ruin as well. Badong and Jianping were overrun by gorge tribes; by now the population had fled and almost no one was left. That spring Youzhi sent an army into the gorges against the tribal leader Tian Wujun and his followers. When Liu Jingsu rebelled, Youzhi hurried after the gorge army. Badong Administrator Liu Rangbing and Jianping Administrator Liu Daoxin both suspected Youzhi of his own designs. They held their forces, sealed the passes, and refused to let his army through. Rangbing's eldest son Tianci was then Western Clerk of Jing Province. Youzhi sent Tianci to reason with his father, telling him to disarm and promising full amnesty.
