When Rangbing saw Tianci, he learned that Jingsu had in fact rebelled. He surrendered his arms and apologized. Youzhi treated him as before and later appointed him headquarters staff secretary. Liu Daoxin held fast to Jianping and would not heed Rangbing's pleas. Rangbing then joined the anti-barbarian force, stormed Jianping, and executed Daoxin.
49
臺直閣高道慶家在江陵，攸之初至州，道慶時在家，牒其親戚十餘人，求州從事西曹，攸之為用三人。 道慶大怒，自入州取教，毀之而去。 及還都，不詣攸之別。 道慶至都，云：「攸之聚眾繕甲，姦逆不久。 」楊運長等常相疑畏，乃與道慶密遣刺客，齎廢帝手詔，以金餅賜攸之州府佐吏，進其階級。 時有象三頭至江陵城北數里，攸之自出格殺之，忽有流矢集攸之馬障泥，其後刺客事發。
Gao Daoqing of the palace Direct Attendant Office was from Jiangling. When Youzhi first took up his post, Daoqing was home on leave. He submitted a list of more than a dozen relatives seeking provincial clerkships. Youzhi appointed three. Daoqing flew into a rage, marched into the provincial office, seized the appointment order, tore it to pieces, and walked out. On returning to the capital, he did not even call on Youzhi to say goodbye. Once in the capital, Daoqing reported: "Youzhi is mustering men and forging arms; rebellion is not far off. " Yang Yunchang and his circle had long feared and distrusted Youzhi. Together with Daoqing they secretly sent assassins bearing the deposed emperor's personal edict, awarding gold ingots to Youzhi's staff and promoting their ranks. Three elephants appeared a few li north of Jiangling. Youzhi rode out and killed them himself. A stray arrow suddenly struck the mudguard of his saddle; only later did the assassination plot come to light.
50
廢帝既殞，順帝即位，進攸之號車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加班劍二十人。 遣攸之長子司徒左長史元琰齎廢帝刳斮之具以示攸之。 元琰既至江陵，攸之便有異志，腹心議有不同，故其事不果。 其年十一月，乃發兵反叛。 攸之素蓄士馬，資用豐積，至是戰士十萬，鐵馬二千。 遣使要雝州刺史張敬兒、梁州刺史范伯年、司州刺史姚道和、湘州行事庾佩玉、巴陵內史王文和等。 敬兒、文和斬其使，馳表以聞； 伯年、道和、佩玉懷兩端，密相應和。
After the deposed emperor's death, Emperor Shun took the throne. Youzhi was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with ducal protocol and twenty ceremonial swords. They sent Youzhi's eldest son Yuanyan, senior clerk of the left in the Secretariat, carrying the tools of the deposed emperor's dismemberment to show his father. When Yuanyan reached Jiangling, Youzhi was already plotting rebellion, but his inner circle was divided and the plan came to nothing. That November he took up arms in open rebellion. Youzhi had long been hoarding troops, horses, and supplies. He now fielded a hundred thousand soldiers and two thousand armored cavalry. He sent envoys to win over Zhang Jing'er of Yong, Fan Bonian of Liang, Yao Daohé of Si, Yu Peiyu acting for Xiang, Wang Wenhe of Baling, and others. Jing'er and Wenhe executed the envoys and raced dispatches to the court; Bonian, Daohé, and Peiyu hedged their bets and secretly signaled their support.
51
十二月十二日，攸之遣其輔國將軍、中兵參軍、督前鋒軍事孫同，率寧朔將軍中兵參軍武寶、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱君拔、寧朔將軍沈慧真、龍驤將軍中兵參軍王道起； 又遣司馬、冠軍將軍劉攘兵，率寧朔將軍外兵參軍公孫方平、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱靈寶、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍沈僧敬、龍驤將軍高茂； 又遣輔國將軍中兵參軍王靈秀、輔國將軍中兵參軍丁珍東，率寧朔將軍中兵參軍王珍之、寧朔將軍外兵參軍楊景穆，相繼俱下。 攸之自率輔國將軍錄事參軍兼司馬武茂宗、輔國將軍中兵參軍沈韶、寧朔將軍中兵參軍皇甫賢、寧朔將軍中兵參軍胡欽之、龍驤將軍中兵參軍東門道順，閏十二月四日至夏口。 攸之將發江陵，使沙門釋僧桀筮之，曰：「不至京邑，當自郢州回還。 」意甚不悅。 初，江津有雲氣，狀如塵霧，從西北來，正蓋軍上。 至沌口，云：「當問訊安西，暫泊黃金浦。 」既登岸，郢城出軍擊之。 攸之聞齊王世子據盆口，震懾不敢下，因攻郢城。 時齊王輔政，遣眾軍西討。 尚書符征西府曰：
On the twelfth of the twelfth month, Youzhi sent Sun Tong—General Who Assists the State, central army major, and vanguard commander—with Wu Bao, Zhu Junba, Shen Huizhen, and Wang Daoqi; He also sent staff secretary and General Who Conquers the Foe Liu Rangbing with Gongsun Fangping, Zhu Lingbao, Shen Sengjing, and Gao Mao; He further sent Wang Lingxiu and Ding Zhendong with Wang Zhenzhi and Yang Jingmu, who marched down one after another. Youzhi himself led Wu Maozong, Shen Shao, Huangfu Xian, Hu Qinzhi, and Dongmen Daoshun, arriving at Xiakou on the fourth of the intercalary twelfth month. Before leaving Jiangling, Youzhi had the monk Sengjie cast lots. The answer read: "You will not reach the capital; you will turn back from Ying Province. " He was deeply displeased. Earlier, at the Jiang crossing a cloud like dust and mist rolled in from the northwest and settled directly over his army. At Dunkou he announced: "We shall inquire after the Pacifier of the West and anchor briefly at Golden Harbor. " Once ashore, the garrison at Ying sallied out against him. Learning that the Prince of Qi's heir held Pankou, Youzhi lost his nerve and would not advance, and instead laid siege to Ying. The Prince of Qi was then regent and sent the main armies west against him. The Secretariat issued this order to the western campaign headquarters:
52
尊冠賤屨，君臣之位，奉順忌逆，成敗斯兆，未有憑陵我郊圻，侵軼我河縣，而不焚師殪甲，靡旗亂轍者也。 沈攸之少長庸賤，擢自閻伍，邀百戰之運，乘一捷之功，鐫山裂地，腰金扡紫，窮貴於國，極富於家。 擁旄蕃伯，便無北面之禮； 受督志屏，即有專征之釁。 橘柚不薦，璆{王替}罕入，箕賦深斂，毒被南郢，枉繩矯墨，害著西荊，饕餮其心，谿壑其性，從始至終，沿壯得老。 今遂驅迫妖黨，繕集尪卒，結釁外城，送死中甸，是而可忍，孰不可懷！
The cap ranks above the sandal—that is the order of ruler and subject. Loyalty brings success; rebellion brings ruin. No army that tramples our borders and violates our river counties has ever escaped with its forces burned, its armor shattered, its banners strewn, and its tracks in chaos. Shen Youzhi rose from common streets and alleys. He seized the luck of a hundred battles and parlayed one victory into carved mountains and split domains, gold at his belt and purple at his side, until he stood at the summit of state rank and household wealth. Made a frontier lord with his own banner, he no longer observed the rites owed the throne; once given command he turned his back on duty, and the signs of independent war-making appeared at once. He sent no tribute of citrus or fine jade. He taxed the people to the bone, and southern Ying reeled under his cruelty. He perverted law and justice, and western Jing bore the scars. His heart was insatiable, his appetite a bottomless gorge. From first to last he grew ever bolder with age. Now he drives his wicked followers, musters a rabble, raises rebellion beyond the walls, and marches them to die in the heartland. If this can be tolerated, what outrage cannot?
53
今遣新除使持節、督郢州之義陽諸軍事、平西將軍、郢州刺史、聞喜縣開國侯黃回、員外散騎常侍、冠軍、驍騎將軍、南臨淮太守、重安縣開國子、軍主王敬則、輔國將軍、屯騎校尉、長壽縣開國男王宜與、輔國將軍、南高平太守、軍主陳承叔、輔國將軍、左軍將軍、南濮陽太守、葛陽縣開國男、軍主彭文之、龍驤將軍、驃騎行參軍、軍主召宰，精甲二萬，前鋒雲騰。 又遣散騎常侍、領游擊將軍、湘南縣開國男、新除使持節、督湘州諸軍事、征虜將軍、湘州刺史、軍主呂安國、屯騎校尉、寧朔將軍崔慧景、輔國將軍、軍主任候伯、輔國將軍、驍騎將軍、軍主蕭順之、輔國將軍、游擊將軍、軍主垣崇祖、寧朔將軍、虎賁中郎將、軍主尹略、屯騎校尉、南城令曹虎頭，舳艫二萬，駱驛繼邁。 又遣輔國將軍、後軍將軍、右軍中兵參軍事、軍主苟元賓、寧朔將軍、撫軍中兵參軍事、軍主郭文孝、龍驤將軍、撫軍中兵參軍事、軍主程隱雋，輕艓一萬，截其津要。 新除持節督廣、交、越、寧、湘州之廣興諸軍事、領平越中郎將、征虜將軍、廣州刺史、統馬軍主、沌陽縣開國子周盤龍、輔國將軍、後軍統馬軍主張文憘、龍驤將軍、軍主薛道淵、冠軍將軍、游擊將軍、并州刺史、南清河太守、太原公、軍主王敕勤、龍驤將軍、射聲校尉王洪軌、龍驤將軍、冗從僕射、軍主成置等，鐵馬五千，龍驤後陳。 凡此諸帥，莫不勇力動天，勁志駕日，接衝拔距，鷹瞵鶚視，顧盼則前後風生，喑嗚則左右電起，以此攻城，何城不克，以此赴敵，何陳能堅。 然後鑾戎薄臨，龍虎百萬，六軍齊軌，五輅舒斾，丹檻發照，素甲生波，樓煩白羽，投鞍成岳，漁陽墨騎，浴鐵為群，芝艾同焚，悔將何及。
We now dispatch Huang Hui, newly appointed inspector of Ying with command over Yiyang, General Who Pacifies the West, and Marquis of Wenxi; Wang Jingze, supernumerary attendant, General Who Conquers the Foe, Administrator of South Linhuai, and Viscount of Chong'an; Wang Yiyu, General Who Assists the State and Baron of Changshou; Chen Chengshu of South Gaoping; Peng Wenzhi of South Puyang and Baron of Geyang; and Shao Zai of the Dragon Cavalry—with twenty thousand elite troops, the vanguard thundering forward. We also send Lu Anguo, inspector of Xiang with command as General Who Campaigns against the Barbarians and Baron of Xiangnan; Cui Huijing; Ren Houbo; Xiao Shunzhi; Yuan Chongzu; Yin Lue; and Cao Hutou—with twenty thousand warships advancing in unbroken columns. We also send Gou Yuanbin, Guo Wenxiao, and Cheng Yinjuan with ten thousand light craft to seize the crossings and choke points. We further send Zhou Panlong of Guang, Zhang Wenxi, Xue Daoyuan, Wang Chiqin of Bing and Duke of Taiyuan, Wang Honggui, and Cheng Zhi—with five thousand armored cavalry as the dragon rear guard. Every one of these commanders possesses strength that shakes heaven and spirit that outruns the sun. They meet the battering ram and hold the walls, glare like hunting birds, and at a glance wind rises before and behind; at a shout lightning strikes left and right. What city could stand against such attackers? What battle line could hold against them? Then the imperial host will close in: a million dragon-and-tiger soldiers, the Six Armies in one column, the five imperial chariots with banners unfurled, red rails blazing, white armor rippling like water, Loufan arrows piled mountain-high, Yuyang black cavalry massed in iron ranks. Good and bad will burn together—then regret will come too late.
54
符到之日，幸加三省。 其鋒陳營壁之主，驅逼寇手之人，若有投命軍門，一無所問。 或能因罪立績，終不爾欺，斬裾射玦，唯功是與。 能斬送攸之首，封三千戶縣公，賜布、絹各五千匹。 信如河海，皎然無貳。 飛火軍攝文書，千里驛行。 齊王出頓新亭，馳檄數攸之罪惡，曰：
When this order reaches you, consider it well. Commanders of the rebel vanguard and men forced into his ranks who surrender at our gates will not be questioned. Those who redeem their crimes with service will not be cheated: as with severing the skirt or shooting the jade ring, reward will follow merit alone. Whoever delivers Youzhi's head will be made a district duke of three thousand households and given five thousand bolts of cloth and five thousand of silk. Our word is as broad as the rivers and seas, clear and without deceit. The Flying Fire Army bears this dispatch, relayed a thousand li by post. The Prince of Qi encamped at Xinting and issued a swift proclamation listing Youzhi's crimes, declaring:
55
夫彎弓射天，未見能至； 揮戈擊地，多力安施。 何則？ 逆順之勢定殊，禍福之驗易原也。 是以違乎天者，鬼神不能使其成； 會乎人者，聖哲不能令其毀。 故劉濞賴七國連兵之勢，隗囂恃跨河據隴之資，毋丘儉伐其逾海越島之功，諸葛誕矜其待士愛民之德，彼四子者，皆當世雄傑，以犯順取禍，覆窟傾巢，為豎子笑。 況乎行陳凡才，斗筲小器，而懷問鼎之志，敢構無君之逆哉！
To draw a bow and shoot at heaven is to aim at what no arrow can reach; to swing a halberd at the earth is to waste one's strength. Why? The tide of rebellion and loyalty runs in opposite directions, and fortune and ruin are easy to read in advance. He who defies heaven cannot succeed even if ghosts and spirits aid him; he who wins men's hearts cannot be destroyed even by sages. Liu Pi leaned on the Seven States' alliance; Wei Xiao on his hold over the river and Longxi; Wenqiu Jian on his feats beyond the sea; Zhuge Dan on his reputation for honoring scholars and caring for the people. All four were heroes of their day, yet by rebelling they brought ruin on themselves—nests overturned, dens destroyed—and became laughingstocks. What then of a common soldier, a man of petty measure, who dares dream of seizing the throne and plotting rebellion against his lord!
56
逆賊沈攸之，出自萊畝，寂寥累世，故司空沈公以從父宗蔭，愛之若子，卵翼吹噓，得升官秩。 廢帝昏悖，猜畏柱臣，攸之貪競乘機，凶忍趨利，躬行反噬，請銜誅旨。 又攸之與譚金、童太壹等並受寵任，朝為牙爪，同功共體，世號三侯，當時親昵，情過管、鮑。 遭仰革運，凶黨懼戮，攸之狡猾用數，圖全賣禍，既殺從父，又害良朋。 雖呂布販君，酈寄賣友，方之斯人，未足為酷。 此其不信不義，言詐翻覆，諸夏之所未有，夷狄之所不為也。 泰始開闢，網漏吞舟，略其兇險，取其搏噬，故得階亂獲全，因禍保福。 攸之空淺，躁而無謀，濃湖崩挫，本非己力； 及北伐彭、泗，望賊宵奔； 重討下邳，一鼓而遁； 再鄙王師，又應肆法。 先帝英聖，量深河海，宥其回谿之敗，冀收曲崤之捷，故得推遷幸會，頓升崇顯，內端戎禁，外臨方牧。 聖靈鼎湖，遠頒顧命，託寄崇深，義感金石。 而攸之始奉國諱，喜見於容，普天同哀，己以為慶。 此其樂禍幸災，大逆之罪一也。
The rebel Shen Youzhi sprang from the fields, obscure for generations. The late Minister of Works Shen, his father's cousin, loved him as a son, nurtured and promoted him, and raised him to rank and office. When the deposed emperor turned paranoid toward his chief ministers, Youzhi seized the moment—greedy, ruthless, and eager for gain. He personally carried out the killings and asked to execute the imperial order himself. Youzhi, Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and others were all favorites at court—his fangs and claws, bound in shared fortune. They were called the Three Marquises, and their bond surpassed even that of Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya. When the dynasty turned and the guilty feared punishment, Youzhi schemed to save himself by betraying others. He killed his father's cousin and destroyed his closest friends. Lü Bu betrayed his master and Li Ji sold out his friend—but beside this man, even they seem mild. Such faithlessness, such treachery and double-dealing—the civilized realms have never seen it, and even barbarians would not stoop to it. When the Taishi era began, the law was lenient enough to let great offenders slip through. His violence was overlooked and his savagery tolerated, so he survived the turmoil and turned disaster into fortune. Youzhi is shallow, rash, and devoid of strategy. The rout at Nonghu owed nothing to his ability; on the northern campaign against Peng and Si he fled at the sight of the enemy; at the second assault on Xiapi he broke and ran at the first drum; twice he disgraced the imperial army and deserved the full penalty of the law. The late emperor, sage and magnanimous as the rivers and seas, pardoned his defeat at Huiqi in hope of victory at Quqiao. By sheer luck Youzhi was suddenly raised to high rank, commanding the inner guard and governing the frontier. When the late emperor ascended to Dinghu, he entrusted Youzhi from afar with a charge profound as metal and stone. Yet when the nation went into mourning, joy showed on Youzhi's face. While the empire grieved, he rejoiced. This is his first great crime of treason: delighting in calamity and rejoicing in others' suffering.
57
又攸之累登蕃兵，自郢遷荊，晉熙殿下以皇弟代鎮，地尊望重，攸之肆情陵侮，斷割候迎，料擇士馬，簡筭器甲，精器銳士，竝取自隨，郢城所留，十不遺一，專擅略虜，罔顧國典。 此其苞藏禍志，不恭不虔，大逆之罪二也。
Youzhi repeatedly held frontier commands, moving from Ying to Jing. When Prince Jinxi, the emperor's brother, replaced him—a post of high honor—Youzhi insulted and robbed him, seizing the welcoming supplies, cherry-picking troops and arms, and taking every elite soldier and weapon for himself. Ying was left with less than a tenth of its forces. He plundered at will and ignored the laws of the realm. This is his second great crime: harboring treason and showing no respect or loyalty.
58
又攸之踐荊以來，恆用姦數，既欲發兵，宜有因假，遂乃蹙迫群蠻，騷擾山谷，揚聲討伐，盡戶發上，蟻聚郭邑，伺國盛衰，從來積年，永不解甲。 遂使四野百縣，路無男人； 耕田載租，皆驅女弱。 自古酷虐，未聞有此。 其侮蔑朝廷，大逆之罪三也。
Since taking Jing, Youzhi has constantly schemed. Wanting to raise an army, he needed a pretext, so he harried the tribal peoples, roiled the valleys, and proclaimed campaigns of suppression. He conscripted every household until the towns swarmed with soldiers watching the court's fortunes. For years they have never stood down. Across the countryside and through a hundred districts, no man was to be seen on the roads; plowing and hauling tribute fell entirely to women and the weak. Never in history has such cruelty been heard of. This is his third great crime: contempt for the court.
59
去昔桂陽奇兵□起，京師內{畾大}，宗廟阽危。 攸之任居上流，兵強地廣，救援顛沛，實宜悉力。 國家倒懸，方思身慮，威遣弱卒三千，竝皆羸老，使就郢州，稟受節度，欲令判否之日，委罪晉熙。 何其平日輈張，實輕周、邵，爾時恭謹，虛重皇戚。 此其伏慝藏詐，持疑兩端，大逆之罪四也。
When the Guiyang surprise force rose not long ago, the capital was thrown into alarm and the ancestral temple teetered on the brink. Youzhi held the upper Yangtze, with strong troops and broad territory. He should have thrown every resource into saving the court in its hour of peril. With the state in mortal danger, he sent only three thousand weak and aged soldiers to Ying to take orders—planning, when the outcome was decided, to shift the blame onto Prince Jinxi. How arrogant he is in ordinary times, treating the realm's pillars with contempt—yet then he played the dutiful subject, feigning reverence for the imperial house. This is his fourth great crime: hiding malice, concealing deceit, and hedging between two sides.
60
又攸之累據方州，跋扈滋甚，招誘輕狡，往者咸納； 羈絆行侶，過境必留。 仕子窮困，不得歸其鄉； 商人畢命，無由還其土。 叛亡入境，輒加擁護； 逋逃出界，必遣窮追。 此其大逆之罪五也。
Youzhi has long held frontier provinces, growing ever more arrogant. He welcomes every reckless adventurer who comes his way; he detains travelers and keeps everyone who passes through his territory. Officials' sons, stranded and destitute, cannot return home; merchants risk their lives and cannot get back to their own lands. Deserters and fugitives who enter his territory are sheltered at once; those who flee his domain are hunted without mercy. This is his fifth great crime of treason.
61
又攸之自任專恣，恃行慘酷，視吏若仇，遇民如草。 峻太半之賦，暴參夷之刑。 鞭捶國士，全用虜法； 一人逃亡，闔宗補代。 毒遍嬰孩，虐加斑白。 獄囚恆滿，市血常流。 男不得耕，女不得織。 奔馳道路，號哭動天。 皇朝赦令，初不遵奉，欲殺欲擊，故曠蕩之澤，長隔彼州。 此其無君陵上，大逆之罪六也。
Youzhi rules by whim and cruelty, treating officials as enemies and common people like weeds. He levies taxes above half the harvest and inflicts punishments extending to three generations. He flogs men of rank with barbarian methods; if one man flees, his entire clan is conscripted in his place. His cruelty reaches infants; his oppression extends to the aged. The prisons are always full; blood flows constantly in the marketplace. Men cannot farm; women cannot weave. People flee along the roads, their wailing shaking the heavens. He ignores the court's amnesties, killing and beating at will, so the emperor's mercy never reaches his province. This is his sixth great crime of treason: disloyalty to his sovereign and contempt for authority above him.
62
蒼梧狂凶，釁深桀、紂，猜貳外蕃，鴞目西顧。 留其長息元琰，以為交質； 父子分張，彌積年稔。 賴社稷靈長，獨夫遄戮，攸之豫稟心靈，宜同歡幸。 遂迷惑顛倒，深相嗟惜。 舉言哀桀，揚聲吠堯。 此其不辨是非，罔識善惡，違情背理，大逆之罪七也。
The Deposed Emperor was violent and depraved, his crimes surpassing even Jie and Zhou; distrustful of the frontier lords, he turned his predatory gaze westward. He kept his eldest son Yuan Yan as a hostage to guarantee good faith; Father and son remained apart, year after year. By the enduring grace of the dynasty, the tyrant was swiftly put to death; Youzhi had long known this in his heart and should have rejoiced with the rest. Instead he grew confused and perverse, deeply mourning the fallen tyrant. He spoke as though mourning Jie, and raised his voice to snarl at Yao. This is his seventh great crime of treason: blindness to right and wrong, ignorance of good and evil, and defiance of all reason and decency.
63
廢昏立明，先代盛典，交、廣先到，梁、秦蚤及，而攸之密邇內畿，川塗弗遠，驛書至止，晏若不聞，未遣章表，奄積旬朔。 防風後至，夏典所誅，此其大逆之罪八也。
Deposing the unworthy and enthroning the worthy is a sacred precedent of former dynasties. Jiao and Guang submitted first; Liang and Qin soon followed. Yet Youzhi lay close to the capital, with rivers and roads near at hand—when imperial dispatches arrived he acted as though deaf, sent no memorial in reply, and let weeks and months slip by. Fangfeng arrived late and was executed under the laws of Xia—this is his eighth great crime of treason.
64
昇明肇曆，恩深澤遠，申其父子之情，矜其骨肉之恩，馳遣元琰，銜使西歸，竝加崇授，寵貴重疊。 元琰達西，便應反命，攸之得此集聚，蒙誰之恩？ 不荷盛德，反生仇釁，此其大逆之罪九也。
When the Shengming reign began, imperial grace ran deep and far; honoring the bond between father and son and showing compassion for family ties, the court sent Yuan Yan west with envoys, heaping rank and favor upon him. Yuan Yan reached the west and should have reported back—yet Youzhi assembles this host; by whose grace does he act? He repaid great kindness with enmity and rebellion—this is his ninth great crime of treason.
65
攸之以谿壑之性，含梟鴆之腸，直置天壤，已稱醜穢。 況乃舉兵內侮，逞肆奸回，斯實惡熟罪成之辰，決癰潰疽之日。 幕府過荷朝寄，義百常憤，董司元戎，龔行天罰。 今皇上聖明，將相仁厚，約法三章，輕刑緩賦，年登歲阜，家給人足，上有惠和之澤，下無樂亂之心。 攸之不識天時，妄圖奸逆，舉無名之師，驅怨仇之黨。 是以朝野審其易取，含識判其成禽。 熊羆厲爪，蓄攫裂之心； 虎豹摩牙，起吞噬之憤。 鼓怒則冰原激電，奮發則霜野奔靁，以此定亂，豈移晷刻。 雖復眾徒梗陸，舉郡阻川，何足以抗沸海之濤，當燒山之焰。
Youzhi's nature is insatiable as a gorge, his heart venomous as an owl's; standing between heaven and earth, he is already counted foul and vile. Now he raises arms against the realm and indulges his treachery—this is the hour when his wickedness has fully ripened, the day to lance the abscess and drain the poison. The command bears heavy trust from the court, righteous wrath ever burning; it directs the grand army and reverently executes heaven's punishment. The emperor is sage and enlightened, his generals and ministers benevolent; laws are simple, punishments light, and taxes eased. Harvests are plentiful, households prosper, and the people want for nothing. Grace flows from above, and none below wish for rebellion. Youzhi fails to read heaven's signs, vainly plotting treason, raising an army without just cause and driving a mob of the resentful and desperate. Court and countryside alike see him as easy prey; all who understand the situation know he will be captured. Bears and grizzlies sharpen their claws, hearts set on tearing their prey apart; tigers and leopards grind their teeth, wrath rising to devour. When wrath is roused, lightning sears the frozen plains; when they strike, thunder rolls across the frost— with such force to quell rebellion, not a moment need pass. Even if his troops block the land and whole commanderies hold the rivers, how can they withstand the boiling sea or match the flame that burns mountains?
66
彼土士民，罹毒日久，逃竄無路，常所憫然。 今復相逼，起接鋒刃，交戰之日，蘭艾難分。 土崩倒戈，宜為蚤計，無使一人迷昧，而九族就禍也。 弘宥之典，有如皎日。
The gentry and common people of that region have long suffered his cruelty, fleeing with nowhere to go—the court has always pitied them. Now they are driven again to face the blade; on the day of battle, the innocent and the guilty will be impossible to tell apart. Collapse and mutiny should be foreseen in time—do not let one man's folly bring disaster upon nine generations of kin. The charter of broad pardon shines clear as the noonday sun.
67
攸之盡銳攻郢州，行事柳世隆隨宜距應，屢摧破之。 攸之與武陵王贊箋曰：「江陵一緫八州，地居形勝，鎮撫之重，宜以上歸。 本欲仰移節蓋，改臨荊部，所以未具上聞者，欲待至止，面自咨申。 不圖重關擊柝，覲接莫由。 若使匡朝之誠，終蔽於聖察，襲遠之舉，近擁於郢都，則無以謝烈士之心，何用塞義夫之志，便不犯關陵漢，期一接奉。 若夫斬蛟陷石之卒，裂骼卷鐵之將，煙騰飆迅，容或驚動左右，苟不獲已，敢不先布下情。 」又曰：「下官位重分陝，富兼金穴，子弟勝衣，爵命已及，親黨辨菽，抽序便加，耳倦弦歌，口厭粱肉，布衣若此，復欲何求？ 豈不知俛眉苟安，保養餘齒，何為不計百口，甘冒危難。 誠感歷朝之遇，欲報之於皇家爾。 昧理之徒，謂下官懷無厭之願，既貫誠於白日，不復明心於殿下。 若使天必喪道，忠節不立，政復闔門碎滅，百死無恨。 但高祖王業艱難，太祖劬勞日昃，卜世不盡七百之期，宗社已成他人之有。 家國之事，未審於聖心何如？」
Youzhi threw his full strength against Ying Province; Acting Administrator Liu Shilong met him as circumstances required and repeatedly defeated him. Youzhi wrote to Prince Zan of Wuling: "Jiangling commands eight provinces and occupies commanding ground—the responsibility of guarding and pacifying it ought to rest with the throne above." "I had meant to defer moving my command and take up oversight of Jing instead; I had not yet reported fully to the throne because I wished to wait until I arrived and explain in person." "I did not expect barred passes and watchmen's clappers—I have no way to gain an audience." "If my loyalty to restore the dynasty remains hidden from your sacred discernment, and my long march is hemmed in at Ying's walls, I cannot answer my loyal soldiers or satisfy men of honor—I shall force the passes and cross the Han, hoping only for one audience." "As for soldiers who can slay dragons and shatter stone, generals who can rend bone and wield iron—with smoke rising and winds swift—they may startle those around you; if there is no other way, how dare I not first explain my position." " He also wrote: "Your humble servant's rank equals the partition of Shan, my wealth rivals the golden vaults; my sons and brothers are grown, titles and commands already granted; kin and allies receive promotion at every turn; my ears are weary of music, my mouth sated with fine fare—a man of plain cloth such as I, what more could I want?" "Does your humble servant not know to bow his head and live in peace, preserving his remaining years? Why would he, without regard for a hundred mouths to feed, willingly court such danger?" "It is only gratitude for the grace of successive reigns, and a wish to repay the imperial house—that is all." "Men who fail to understand say your humble servant harbors boundless ambition; but having pledged my loyalty before the bright sun, I need not prove my heart again to Your Highness." "If heaven has abandoned the Way and loyalty cannot prevail, then even if my whole household is destroyed, I would die a hundred deaths without regret." "Only—the Founding Emperor's enterprise was won through hardship; the Grand Ancestor toiled from dawn till dusk; the dynasty was not granted its full span of seven hundred years—the altars of state have passed to another's hands." "As for the affairs of house and state—I know not what Your Majesty's sacred heart thinks of them."
68
攸之遣中兵參軍公孫方平馬步三千向武昌，太守臧渙棄郡投西陽太守王毓，奔於盆口，方平因據西陽。 建寧太守張謨率二守千人攻之，方平破走。 攸之攻郢城久不決，眾心離沮。 昇明二年正月十九日夜，劉攘兵燒營入降郢城，眾於是離散，不可復制。 將曉，攸之斬劉天賜，率大眾過江，至魯山，諸軍因此散走。 還向江陵，未百餘里，聞城已為雍州刺史張敬兒所據，無所歸，乃與第三子中書侍郎文和至華容界，為封人所斬送。
Youzhi sent Central Army Major Gongsun Fangping with three thousand horse and foot toward Wuchang. Prefect Zang Huan abandoned his command and joined Xiyang Prefect Wang Yu, fleeing to Pankou; Fangping then occupied Xiyang. Jianning Prefect Zhang Mo led a thousand men from two commanderies to attack him; Fangping was defeated and fled. Youzhi's siege of Ying city dragged on without success, and morale collapsed. On the night of the nineteenth day of the first month of the second year of Shengming, Liu Rangbing burned his camp and surrendered to Ying city; the army then scattered beyond control. Near dawn, Youzhi executed Liu Tianci, led his main force across the river to Lushan, and the armies thereupon scattered and fled. Turning back toward Jiangling, before he had gone a hundred li, he learned the city was already held by Yong Province Inspector Zhang Jing'er. With nowhere to go, he and his third son, Secretariat Gentleman Wenhe, reached the border of Huarong, where frontier guards beheaded them and sent in their heads.
69
攸之晚好讀書，手不釋卷，《史》、《漢》事多所諳憶，常歎曰：「早知窮達有命，恨不十年讀書。 」及攻郢城，夜遇風浪，米船沉沒，倉曹參軍崔靈鳳女幼適柳世隆子，攸之正色謂曰：「當今軍糧要急，而卿不以在意，將由與城內婚姻邪？ 」靈鳳答曰：「樂廣有言，下官豈以五男易一女。 」攸之歡然意解。
In his later years Youzhi loved reading and never let a scroll leave his hand; he knew much of the Records and the History from memory, and often sighed: "Had I known early that fortune and failure are fated, I would regret not having spent ten years reading." " When assaulting Ying city, they met wind and waves by night and grain boats sank. Army Provision Master Cui Lingfeng's young daughter had married Liu Shilong's son; Youzhi said sternly: "Military grain is urgent, yet you pay it no heed—is it because of marriage ties with those inside the city?" " Lingfeng replied: "As Yue Guang once said—would your humble servant trade five sons for one daughter?" " Youzhi was pleased, and his suspicion cleared.
70
初，攸之招集才力之士，隨郡人雙泰真有幹力，召不肯來。 後泰真至江陵賣買，有以告攸之者，攸之因留之，補隊副，厚加料理。 泰真無停志，少日叛走，攸之遣二十人被甲追之，逐討甚急。 泰真殺數人，餘者不敢近。 欲過家將母去，事迫不獲，單身走入蠻； 追者既失之，錄其母而去。 泰真既失母，乃出自歸，攸之不罪，曰：「此孝子也。 」賜錢一萬，轉補隊主，其矯情任笇皆如此。
Earlier, Youzhi gathered men of talent and strength; Shuang Taizhen of Suixian was capable, but when summoned he refused to come. Later Taizhen came to Jiangling on business; someone informed Youzhi, who detained him, made him deputy squad leader, and treated him generously. Taizhen's resolve to leave never ceased; within days he rebelled and fled. Youzhi sent twenty armored men in pursuit, pressing the chase relentlessly. Taizhen killed several of them; the rest dared not approach. He wished to stop at home and take his mother away, but pressed by events he could not, and fled alone into the barbarian lands; The pursuers, having lost him, seized his mother and departed. Having lost his mother, Taizhen came out and surrendered. Youzhi did not punish him, saying: "This is a filial son." " He gave him ten thousand cash and promoted him to squad leader—his feigned sentiments and calculated acts were all of this kind.
71
初，攸之賤時，與吳郡孫超之、全景文共乘小船出京都，三人共上引埭，有一人止而相之曰：「君三人皆當至方伯。 」攸之曰：「豈有三人俱有此相？ 」相者曰：「骨法如此，若有不驗，便是相書誤耳。 」其後攸之為郢、荊二州，超之廣州，景文豫州刺史。 攸之初至郢州，有順流之志。 府主簿宗儼之勸攻郢城，功曹臧寅以為：「攻守勢異，非旬日所拔，若不時舉，挫銳損威。 今順流長驅，計日可捷，既傾根本，則郢城豈能自固。 」攸之不從，既敗，諸將帥皆奔散，惟寅曰：「我委質事人，豈可苟免。 我之不負公，猶公之不負朝廷也。 」乃投水死。 寅，字士若，東莞莒人也。
Earlier, when Youzhi was still obscure, he shared a small boat leaving the capital with Sun Chaozhi of Wu commandery and Quan Jingwen; the three together ascended the Yin embankment, where a man stopped and read their faces, saying: "You three will all reach the rank of regional lord." " Youzhi said: "Can all three have such a destiny?" " The physiognomist said: "Your bone structure says so—if it fails to come true, then the books of physiognomy are wrong." " In time Youzhi became governor of Ying and Jing, Chaozhi governor of Guangzhou, and Jingwen Inspector of Yuzhou. When Youzhi first reached Ying Province, he intended to push downstream. Registrar Zong Yanzhi urged an attack on Ying city, but Merit Officer Zang Yin argued: "Attack and defense are not the same—the city cannot be taken in ten days; miss the moment and you blunt your edge and lose prestige." "Drive downstream at speed now—victory can be counted in days; once the root is overturned, how can Ying city hold on alone?" " Youzhi did not listen. After defeat, all the generals scattered—only Yin said: "I pledged myself to serve a lord—how can I seek to escape?" "My loyalty to my lord is like my lord's loyalty to the court." " He threw himself into the water and died. Yin, styled Shiruo, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.
72
先是，攸之在郢州，州從事輒與府錄事鞭，攸之免從事官，而更鞭錄事五十。 謂人曰：「州官鞭府職，誠非體要，由小人凌侮士大夫。 」倉曹參軍事邊榮為府錄事所辱，攸之自為榮鞭殺錄事。 攸之自江陵下，以榮為留府司馬，守城。 張敬兒將至，人或說之使詣敬兒降，榮曰：「受沈公厚恩，共如此大事，一朝緩急，便改易本心，不能行也。 」城敗，見敬兒，敬兒問曰：「邊公何不早來？ 」榮曰：「沈公見留守城，而委城求活，所不忍也。 本不蘄生，何須見問。 」敬兒曰：「死何難得。 」命斬之，歡笑而去，容無異色。 泰山程邕之者，素依隨榮，至是抱持榮曰：「與邊公周遊，不忍見邊公前死，乞見殺。 」兵不得行戮，以告敬兒，敬兒曰：「求死甚易，何為不許。 」先殺邕之，然後及榮。 三軍莫不垂泣，曰：「奈何一日殺二義士。 」比之臧洪及陳容。 榮，金城人也。
Earlier, when Youzhi was at Ying Province, a provincial aide repeatedly flogged the prefectural recorder; Youzhi dismissed the aide but then flogged the recorder fifty strokes himself. He told others: "For provincial officials to flog prefectural staff is truly improper—it comes of petty men bullying gentlemen." " Army Provision Master Bian Rong was insulted by the prefectural recorder; Youzhi himself flogged the recorder to death on Rong's behalf. When Youzhi marched down from Jiangling, he made Rong acting prefectural major to hold the city. When Zhang Jing'er was about to arrive, some urged him to surrender to Jing'er. Rong said: "I received Lord Shen's deep kindness and shared in this great undertaking—at the critical moment to change my heart, I cannot." " The city fell. Brought before Jing'er, he was asked: "Why did Lord Bian not come sooner?" " Rong said: "Lord Shen entrusted me to hold the city, and I abandoned it to save my life—that I could not bear." "I never hoped to live—why ask?" " Jing'er said: "Death is not hard to obtain." " He ordered him beheaded. Rong went laughing, his face unchanged. Cheng Yinzhi of Taishan had long followed Rong; now he embraced Rong and said: "Having traveled with Lord Bian, I cannot bear to see him die before me—I beg to be killed as well." " The soldiers could not execute him and reported to Jing'er, who said: "Seeking death is easy enough—why not grant it?" " He killed Yinzhi first, then Rong. The whole army wept and said: "How can two righteous men be killed in a single day?" " They were compared to Zang Hong and Chen Rong. Rong was a native of Jincheng.
73
廢帝之殞也，攸之欲起兵，問其知星人葛珂之。 珂之曰：「自古起兵，皆候太白。 太白見則成，伏則敗。 昔桂陽以太白伏時舉兵，一戰授首，此近世明驗。 今蕭公廢昏立明，政值太白伏時，此與天合也。 且太白尋出東方，東方利用兵，西方不利。 」故攸之止不反。 及後舉兵，珂之又曰：「今歲星守南斗，其國不可伐。 」攸之不從。 凡同逆丁珍東、孫同、裴茂仲、武茂宗、宗儼之竝伏誅。 攸之表檄文疏，皆儼之詞也。 臧渙詣盆城自歸，今皇帝命斬之。 餘同惡或為亂軍所殺，或遇赦得原。
When the Deposed Emperor died, Youzhi wished to raise troops and consulted his astrologer Ge Kezhi. Kezhi said: "Since antiquity, all who raise troops watch for Venus." When Venus appears, success follows; when it is hidden, defeat follows. Formerly the Prince of Guiyang raised troops while Venus was hidden—one battle and he lost his head. This is a clear lesson from recent times. Now Lord Xiao deposes the unworthy and enthrones the worthy—just when Venus is hidden. This accords with heaven. Moreover Venus will soon emerge in the east; the east favors military action, the west is unfavorable. " Therefore Youzhi held back and did not rebel. When he later raised troops, Kezhi again said: "Jupiter now guards the Southern Dipper—that state cannot be attacked." " Youzhi did not listen. All fellow rebels—Ding Zhendong, Sun Tong, Pei Maozhong, Wu Maozong, and Zong Yanzhi—were executed together. Youzhi's memorials, proclamations, and dispatches were all written by Yanzhi. Zang Huan went to Pencheng to surrender; the present emperor ordered him executed. The remaining accomplices were either killed in the chaos or pardoned by amnesty.
74
史臣曰：臧質雖貪虐夙樹，問望多闕，奉義治流，本無吞噬之志也。 徒欲以幼君弱政，期之於世祖，據有中流，嗣桓、庾之業。 既主異穆、哀，臣皆代黨，雖禮秩外厚，而疑防內深，功高位重，終非自安之地，至於陵天犯順，其出於此乎！ 攸之伺隙西郢，年逾十載，擅命專威，無君已積。 及天厭宋道，鼎運將離，不識代德之紀，獨迷樂推之數，公休既覆其族，攸之亦屠厥身。 夫以釁亂自終，固異代如一也。
The historian writes: Though Zang Zhi had long been known for greed and cruelty and his reputation was poor, in serving righteousness and holding the Yangzi he originally had no ambition to seize the realm. He merely hoped that with a young ruler and a weak court, he might look to Emperor Shizu, hold the middle Yangzi, and inherit the legacy of Huan Wen and Yu Liang. Having backed the rival lords Mu and Ai, with ministers who were all partisans of the succession struggle, he enjoyed lavish honors on the surface while suspicion and restraint ran deep within. High merit and heavy rank were never a ground for lasting security—and his defiance of Heaven and violation of duty surely arose from this. For more than ten years Youzhi watched for his chance in Western Ying, issuing orders on his own and hoarding power until his disregard for the throne had become a settled habit. When Heaven turned against the Song and the mandate was passing away, he failed to read the signs of dynastic change and clung only to the fantasy that the throne could be forced upon him. Gong Xiu had already destroyed his house, and Youzhi too died by the blade. To perish through treason and rebellion is, in every age, much the same.
